entries.name: Climb
entries.text: The ability to ascend steep or vertical surfaces, like a perilous mountainside or the rain-slick wall of a tumbledown townhouse. Climbing can sometimes be used in combat when facing especially monstrous foes — see page 162 for combat movement.

entries.name: Consume Alcohol
entries.text: How well you can handle alcohol without letting it cloud your judgment or render you senseless. Often used to impress those who find the ability to down an unreasonable number of beverages to be praiseworthy.

entries.name: Cool
entries.text: Allows you to remain calm under stress, resist fear in the face of horror, and stick to your convictions. It is generally used to resist the attempts of others to Charm or Intimidate you, or to curtail other Psychological effects (see page 183).

entries.name: Dodge
entries.text: Avoid things through ducking, diving, and moving quickly, and is used extensively to sidestep falling rocks, incoming weapons, and the like. In combat, Dodge is generally used to resist attacks or avoid damage.

entries.name: Drive
entries.text: Maneuvering vehicles — most commonly simple carts and lumbering coaches, but also the more experimental creations of Imperial Engineers — along the roads of the Empire with as little incident as possible.

entries.name: Endurance
entries.text: Called upon when you must endure hardship, withstand deprivation, stand without moving for long periods of time, or survive harsh environments. In particular, Endurance is Tested to resist or recover from various Conditions (see page 184) and helps you recover lost Wounds (see page 170).

entries.name: Entertain
entries.text: Specialisations: Acting, Comedy, Singing, Storytelling. Delight crowds with the spoken word, perhaps by singing, acting, or attempting a few jokes — hopefully entertaining all those within earshot.

entries.name: Evaluate
entries.text: Lets you determine the value of goods. Everybody is assumed to know the relative worth of general items, but Evaluate allows you to identify the value of curious and unique items, recognise forgeries, or spot flaws.

entries.name: Animal Care
entries.text: Care for animals and heal them from disease or injury. A Character with an Advance in this Skill can keep animals healthy under normal conditions without needing to Test. A Test is required to diagnose or resolve problems with animals, such as spotting signs of illness or healing an injury (page 171).

entries.name: Animal Training
entries.text: Specialisations: Demigryph, Dog, Hawk, Horse, Pigeon Your understanding of a particular type of animal, and ability to train them. To train a beast, undertake the Animal Training Endeavour between adventures (see page 196).

entries.name: Art
entries.text: Specialisations: Drawing, Engraving, Mosaics, Painting, Sculpture, Tattooing, Weaving, Writing. Create works of art in your chosen medium. The more SL achieved, the better the quality of the final piece. For complicated or large works of art, an Extended Test may be required.

entries.name: Athletics
entries.text: Your ability to run, jump, move or perform any other general physical activity.

entries.name: Bribery
entries.text: Find someone who is willing to accept a bribe, such as a guild notary to accept forged paperwork or a gate guard to look the other way while you slip inside after nightfall. You can also make a Bribery Test to judge if a particular person could be bribed, and what their price is likely to be.

entries.name: Channelling
entries.text: Specialisations Include: Aqshy, Azyr, Chamon, Dhar, Ghur, Ghyran, Hysh, Magick, Shyish, Ulgu. Ability to call upon and control the various Winds of Magic, solely used with the magic rules. See Chapter 8: Magic for details.

entries.name: Charm
entries.text: Makes people think favourably of you, your opinions, and actions you propose. People won’t necessarily do what you say simply because you’ve passed a Charm Test, but they will at least give you due consideration.

entries.name: Charm Animal
entries.text: Your aptitude for befriending, quickly calming, or subjugating animals. A Charm Animal Test can convince a wild animal to back off, or a guard dog to devour a proffered scrap of meat rather than your arm.

entries.name: Intuition
entries.text: Gives you a feel for your surroundings, to notice when something is wrong, and read people to sense when they are lying or hiding something.

entries.name: Language
entries.text: Specialisations: Bretonnian, Reikspiel, Wastelander, and many more. See page 149. Access to extra languages beyond your native tongue. A single Advance is enough to make yourself understood in that language, but a Test may be required to comprehend complicated discussions. Once you have 4 Advances, you count as fluent and no longer need to make Tests.

entries.name: Leadership
entries.text: Your ability to lead others and command respect. While most often associated with martial situations, a resolute leader can quickly direct a fast response to a fire or other such calamity, and nobles use the Skill frequently to command their lessers.

entries.name: Lore
entries.text: Specialisations: Engineering, Geology, Heraldry, History, Law, Local*, Magic, Metallurgy, Science, Theology. Knowledge of a subject you have been taught or have first-hand knowledge of. Basic facts related to a specific Lore Skill can be recalled easily, with a Test required only to recall obscure or unusual information.

entries.name: Melee
entries.text: Specialisations: Basic, Brawling, Cavalry, Fencing, Flail, Parry, Polearm, Two-handed. Training and experience with a single type of close combat weaponry. Each Melee Specialisation indicates expertise in using a specific class of weapon. If you do not have the correct Specialisation for a weapon, you will usually suffer a penalty when using it — see Chapter 11: Consumer Guide for more.

entries.name: Navigation
entries.text: Allows you to find your way in the wilderness, or across the ocean, using landmarks, stellar bodies, charts, or maps.

entries.name: Outdoor Survival
entries.text: Used to survive in the wild, including the ability to fish, hunt, forage, and build fires and shelters. Experienced survivors are practiced at reading the signs of incoming inclement weather, making do with minimal tools, and noticing the spoor of local beasts.

entries.name: Gamble
entries.text: Measure the likelihood that a bet will pay off, as well as successfully engage in various games of chance. If you wish to improve your chances through cheating, see page 135.

entries.name: Gossip
entries.text: Ferret out interesting and useful news, and spread rumours of your own. Best practised at a town square, inn, well, or other gathering place.

entries.name: Haggle
entries.text: Secure better deals when negotiating with others, when purchasing goods for example. Typically involves an Opposed Haggle Test (page 131).

entries.name: Heal
entries.text: You have been trained to deal with injuries and diseases. A successful Heal Test allows you to diagnose illness, treat a disease, heal wounds or staunch a Bleeding Condition. Full rules for illness, injury, and treatments can be found on page 172.

entries.name: Intimidate
entries.text: Coerce or frighten sentient creatures — generally with an overt threat, though sometimes a subtle implication or even a look is enough.

entries.name: Pray
entries.text: Invoke, appeal to, or otherwise commune with a deity. For more information on using the Pray Skill to seek divine intervention, see Chapter 7: Religion and Belief.

entries.name: Ranged
entries.text: Specialisations: Blackpowder, Bow, Crossbow, Engineering, Entangling, Explosives, Sling, Throwing. Anyone can throw a rock, but it takes training and practice to use weapons like bows, pistols, and throwing knives. Each Ranged Specialisation is specific to a group of ranged weapons. If you do not have the Ranged Specialisation for a weapon you wish to use, refer to Chapter 11: Consumer Guide for the penalties you will suffer when using the weapon.

entries.name: Research
entries.text: Finding useful and frequently obscure knowledge in libraries and other such storehouses of information. Research requires you to have the Read/Write Talent (see page 124). More on what kinds of information you can find and where to start looking can be found on page 150.

entries.name: Ride
entries.text: Specialisations: Demigryph, Griffon, Horse, Pegasus. Proficiency at riding a particular group of animals; Ride (Horse), for example, will let you ride horses, mules, donkeys, and similar. See page 168 for rules on fighting from the back of a mount.

entries.name: Row
entries.text: Your prowess at pulling an oar to move a boat through the water. A Row Test is typically only needed when racing, navigating rapids, desperately avoiding bog octopuses, or similar challenging feats.

entries.name: Sail
entries.text: Operate and manoeuvre a sailing vessel — including knotwork, steering, gauging the wind, and more. Sail is required to operate your own vessel, either alone or as part of a crew. If you are commanding a well trained crew, use Leadership instead.

entries.name: Perception
entries.text: Your ability to notice things with your senses — sight, smell, hearing, touch, taste, and any other senses you may possess, such as magical or inhuman senses.

entries.name: Perform
entries.text: Specialisations: Acrobatics, Clowning, Dancing, Firebreathing, Juggling, Miming, Rope Walking. You have learned a physically demanding art, perhaps as a way to make a living. A successful Perform Test lets you entertain those near enough to see you.

entries.name: Pick Lock
entries.text: You know the mechanisms of locks and how to open them without their proper keys. Many locks are simple affairs made to vex only untutored thieves, while others can be complex dwarf-made mechanisms capable of frustrating all but the most determined plunderer.

entries.name: Play
entries.text: Specialisations: Bagpipe, Lute, Harpsichord, Horn, Violin. Make music with an instrument, hopefully well enough to impress others. A successful Play Test lets you entertain those near enough to hear you.

entries.name: Secret Signs
entries.text: Specialisations: Grey Order, Guild (Any One), Ranger, Scout, Thief, Vagabond. You have been taught how to use clandestine markings only intelligible to members of a select group. Vagabonds might indicate which homeowners are likely to offer alms, thieves may want to indicate territorial markings or warnings, while scouts may want to warn one another about a dangerous monster’s lair nearby (see page 138).

entries.name: Set Trap
entries.text: From a simple snare or bear trap, to more spectacular devices like Von Grizzel’s Thief-render, players are unlikely to venture far in the Old World without encountering traps. The Set Trap Skill measures your ability to set and disarm traps of all varieties.

entries.name: Sleight of Hand
entries.text: Your ability to pick pockets, palm objects, and perform minor tricks of prestidigitation, as well as cheat at games of chance. This Skill is typically Opposed by the Perception Skill of your target.

entries.name: Stealth
entries.text: Specialisations: Rural, Underground, Urban. Move and hide without being detected, blend into a crowd, or otherwise avoid drawing attention to yourself.

entries.name: Swim
entries.text: Moving and staying afloat in water. If you have the Swim Skill, you are automatically presumed to be able to swim freely without a Test. But if you find yourself in difficult currents, racing, or fleeing from a ravenous stirpike, a Test will be required.

entries.name: Track
entries.text: Your ability to follow subtle trails left by others. Track is used to follow and find your target, as well as to hide your trail.

entries.name: Trade
entries.text: Specialisations: Apothecary, Calligrapher, Chandler, Carpenter, Cook, Embalmer, Engineer, Herbalist, Shipwright, Smith, Tanner. Your ability to practice a trade, to create something or provide a service, as well as your knowledge of the relevant lore surrounding your trade.

entries.name: Accurate Shot
entries.text: You are an exceptional shot and know where to shoot an enemy to inflict maximum damage. Your successful Ranged Attacks inflict +1 Damage, or +2 if you took the time to aim (page 167).

entries.name: Acute Sense (Sense)
entries.text: One of your primary five senses is highly developed, allowing you to spot what others miss. You may take Perception Tests to detect normally imperceptible details with the associated sense, as dictated by the GM. For example, you might be able to hear the difference between the cry of one wolf and another, or taste the difference between the exact same vintage of wine bottled on two different days. You may take this Talent multiple times, choosing a new sense each time you do so.

entries.name: Aethyric Attunement
entries.text: Your experience, talent, or training lets you accumulate magical energy with a reduced risk of miscasts. If you would roll on the Minor Miscast Table, you may roll twice and choose whichever result you prefer. You may purchase this Talent a second time to gain the same benefit when rolling on the Major Miscast Table.

entries.name: Alley Cat
entries.text: You are at home in cities, able to move about without drawing attention to yourself and vanish into any crowd. You gain Advantage on Stealth (Urban) Tests, and can figure out the quickest or least noticeable way to get across any town or city you are familiar with without making a Test.

entries.name: Ambidextrous
entries.text: You can use your off-hand far better than most folk, either by training or innate talent. You do not suffer the –2 SL penalty to Tests relying solely on your secondary hand, including attacks made with weapons held in that hand.

entries.name: Animal Affinity
entries.text: Wild animals feel comfortable in your presence, treating you much as they would an otherwise innocuous part of the environment. As long as you do not act aggressively towards them, wild animals will not ordinarily attack you.

entries.name: Arcane Magic (Lore)
entries.text: You either study one of the eight Colour Lores of Magic (Beasts, Death, Fire, Heavens, Life, Light, Metal, or Shadows), a Witch Lore such as Hedgecraft or Witchcraft, or a Dark Lore like Daemonology or Necromancy. Upon learning the Talent, you gain one Spell of your choice from your chosen Lore. You may now memorise additional Spells from your chosen Lore for the following cost in XP. You may normally learn only one Arcane Lore of Magic. Dark Lores are an exception: depending on your path of study (and with the GM’s permission), you may learn a single Dark Lore in addition to one of the other Arcane Lores. You can unlearn this Talent at a cost of 100 XP, but you will immediately lose all Spells linked to the Talent if you do so. Number of Spells XP Cost for a new Spell currently known Up to 5 100 XP 6 to 10 200 XP 11 to 15 300 XP 16 to 20 400 XP 21 and up 500 XP

entries.name: Argumentative
entries.text: You are especially skilled at drawing others into a quagmire of prolonged and frequently pointless argument. When you argue with someone, they must pass a Cool Test, opposed by your Charm, to disengage from a pointless debate with you. While arguing they are distracted, suffering a -3 SL penalty to most Tests unrelated to you, unless a more important issue is brought to their attention, or they are attacked.

entries.name: Artistic (Art)
entries.text: You have a natural talent for art. You may always advance the Art Skill, even if it is not part of your current Career. When you choose this Talent, pick one form of written or representative art, such as painting or poetry. You gain Advantage on Art Tests when working in that medium. You may purchase this Talent more than once, choosing another art form in which to excel.

entries.name: Attractive
entries.text: Whether it is your piercing eyes or the flash of your perfect teeth, you know how to make the best use of what the gods gave you. When you successfully use Charm to influence those attracted to you, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die.

entries.name: Battle Rage
entries.text: You are always on the edge of self-control, ready to slip into a violent Frenzy at any moment (see page 184). If another ability would allow you to enter a state of Frenzy, you may do so without making a Test. Furthermore, when you exit the Frenzy state, you do not incur a Fatigued Condition.

entries.name: Beat Blade
entries.text: You are trained to make sharp, controlled blows to your opponent’s weapon, creating an opening for an attack. Upon a successful Melee Attack, you may choose to forgo inflicting any Damage. If you do so, your opponent may not Oppose further Melee Tests with any Melee Skill until the end of their next Turn, and Melee Attacks made against them gain the benefit of Advantage. They may continue to oppose attacks with the Dodge Skill. This Talent is of no use if your opponent has a larger Size than you (see page 360).

entries.name: Beneath Notice
entries.text: You are adept at blending into situations that involve your social betters, fading into the background by showing deference to those who think themselves above you. As long as you are properly attired and make some effort to fit in, most people will simply assume you are meant to be there. Gate guards and the like may ask your business, but any plausible explanation is sufficient for them to grant you passage. This Talent affords no protection if you do something to draw attention to yourself such as fumbling a plate full of drinking cups or brandishing a weapon.

entries.name: Berserk Charge
entries.text: You hurl yourself at your enemies with reckless abandon, using the force of your charge to add weight to your strike. When you Charge, add +2 Damage to your strike.

entries.name: Blather
entries.text: You are adept at offering effortless, entirely false justifications for being somewhere you shouldn’t be, or doing something you shouldn’t be doing. When you are caught, make a Charm Test, Opposed by your target’s Cool. If you pass, your preposterous explanation convinces them for one Turn (or minute, depending on the situation) per SL you achieved on the Opposed Test. If you achieved a number of SL greater than your target’s Willpower Bonus, they remain convinced until someone else points out the incongruity in your explanation.

entries.name: Bless (Deity)
entries.text: You are watched over by one of the gods and can empower simple prayers. Upon learning the Talent, you manifest all the Blessings of the deity you worship. Under normal circumstances, you may not learn more than one Bless (Deity) Talent. Further, you may not learn the Channelling Skill or the Arcane Magic, Chaos Magic, Magic Resistance, Petty Magic, or Witch! Talents when you have the Bless Talent, and vice versa. You can unlearn this Talent for 100 XP, but will lose all of your Blessings if you do so, and may garner the disfavour of the god you have spurned, with effects determined by your GM.

entries.name: Bookish
entries.text: You are an avid reader, and know how to quickly navigate your way around a library. You gain Advantage on any Research Test you make.

entries.name: Break and Enter
entries.text: Just by observing a building, locked room, or vault, you can determine what looks to be the fastest and quietest route in. Additionally, you have Advantage on Pick Lock Tests, or Strength Tests made to force open doors or windows.

entries.name: Briber
entries.text: You need only share a few words with someone to know if they are open to a bribe, and exactly how much would be required to have them turn a blind eye, or even assist in some nefarious activity. You have Advantage on any Bribery Test you make.

entries.name: Cardsharp
entries.text: You are used to playing, and winning, at games, although your methods may involve a little cheating. When making an Opposed Gamble Test, if you roll a double, you may reroll your opponent’s Test. This additionally negates any benefit your opponent may have gained with Sleight of Hand.

entries.name: Careful Strike
entries.text: You are skilled at hitting your enemy exactly where you want to. When making a Melee Attack, the penalty for making a Called Shot is reduced to -1 SL. If your attack is made with Advantage, you may make a Called Shot at no penalty.

entries.name: Carouser
entries.text: You are a seasoned drinker and know how to party hard. You do not suffer any ill effects from consuming modest amounts of alcohol, and only need to make a Consume Alcohol Test if drinking to excess — for example, if attempting to impress a bar full of dwarfs. You gain Advantage on any Consume Alcohol Test you make, as well as any Endurance Test you make to resist the effects of poison.

entries.name: Catfall
entries.text: You are as nimble and balanced as a cat. Whenever you fall, it counts as a deliberate fall, allowing you to make an Athletics Test to reduce any Damage incurred. You also gain Advantage on Athletics Tests made while falling.

entries.name: Cat-tongued
entries.text: Like Ranald the Trickster God, you blend truth and lies as if there were no difference. You gain Advantage on any Charm Test you make to lie convincingly.

entries.name: Chaos Magic (Lore)
entries.text: By accident or design, you have lost a portion of your soul to one of the Dark Gods, and can now practise the foul magics of Chaos. Your ruinous patron immediately grants you access to Spells from the chosen Chaos Lore. Upon learning the Talent, you gain one Spell of your choice from your chosen Lore. You may now memorise additional Spells from your chosen Lore for the following cost in XP. Each time you obtain a Spell of your chosen Lore, you gain a Corruption Point as the spell infiltrates your mind, never to be forgotten. Under normal circumstances, you may not learn more than one Lore of Chaos. Unlike the Arcane Lore Talent, once learned, this Talent may never be unlearned. Number of Spells XP Cost for a new Spell currently known Up to 5 100 XP 6 to 10 200 XP 11 to 15 300 XP 16 to 20 400 XP 21 and up 500 XP

entries.name: Combat Aware
entries.text: You are used to scanning the battlefield to make snap decisions informed by the shifting tides of war. You may take a Challenging (+0 SL) Perception Test to avoid gaining the Surprised Condition. If the GM would normally allow a Test to ignore Surprise in this circumstance, you automatically succeed.

entries.name: Combat Master
entries.text: You are adept at making your presence felt on the battlefield, using your size or speed to corner your opponents. You count as two people for the purposes of outnumbering an opponent, or when determining if your side is outnumbered. See page 167 for the rules for outnumbering.

entries.name: Combat Reflexes
entries.text: You react quickly to danger, leaping to attack your enemy without pause. When you roll for Combat Initiative, roll twice and choose your prefered result.

entries.name: Commanding Presence
entries.text: Your presence inspires awe and admiration. In the absence of recognised authority, most people naturally look to you for leadership in a crisis and follow any reasonable orders you give. In addition, you gain Advantage on Leadership Tests.

entries.name: Concoct
entries.text: You are skilled at making potions and draughts on the go. You may make a free Crafting Endeavour each session to use Trade (Apothecary, Herbalist, or Poisoner) without the need for a Workshop. Trade Tools and raw materials are still required. Due to the rushed nature of the creation, it expires at the start of the next Downtime, regardless of whether the item has been completed or not.

entries.name: Contortionist
entries.text: You can bend and manipulate your body in a myriad of seemingly unnatural ways. This allows you to squeeze through gaps that would normally be difficult or impossible, at the GM’s discretion. You gain Advantage on any Athletics Test made to escape from bonds.

entries.name: Coolheaded
entries.text: Gain +5 Willpower. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Crack the Whip
entries.text: You know how to get the most out of your animals. Assuming you have the Drive Skill, you can direct your vehicle’s animals to take an Action, as well as a Move, without a Test. When a Drive Test is required, make it with Advantage. When driving a vehicle in a Pursuit, add +1 to the animals’ Movement Attributes.

entries.name: Craftsman (Trade)
entries.text: You are a true creative talent, sufficiently skilled in a craft to have the potential to elevate it to an art form. Choose a Trade Specialisation. You gain Advantage on Tests of this skill, and may Advance it even if it is not part of your current Career. You may purchase this Talent more than once, choosing a new Trade Specialisation each time you do.

entries.name: Criminal
entries.text: You are an active criminal making money from illegal sources, and you are not always quiet about it. When you successfully use the Income Endeavour to earn coin from a criminal enterprise of any kind, double the resulting coin. Whether through distinctive tattoos, shifty looks, or a rough demeanour, your criminal nature is hard to hide. Law enforcers are naturally suspicious of you and your motives, while other criminals recognise you as a fellow scoundrel. You cannot enter a Career whose Career Path lacks the Criminal Talent. With GM consent, you may spend 100 XP to remove the Criminal Talent.

entries.name: Deadeye Shot
entries.text: You always hit an opponent right between the eyes, or wherever else you intend to hit. When making a Ranged Attack, the penalty for making a Called Shot is reduced to -1 SL, or removed entirely if you are making an aimed shot (page 167).

entries.name: Dealmaker
entries.text: You are a skilled businessman who knows how to close a deal. You gain Advantage on any Haggle Test you make, and usually have a good idea of when an offer really is final.

entries.name: Detect Artefact
entries.text: You are able to sense when magic lies within an artefact. You can automatically tell if an item contains magical energy merely by touching it. If you also possess the Second Sight Talent, you may attempt an Intuition Test to determine the exact powers, means of activation, and number of charges the item possesses.

entries.name: Dicer
entries.text: You are a gaming master, so skilled and lucky in most games of chance that you are frequently accused of cheating, despite rarely needing to. You gain Advantage on any Gamble Test you make.

entries.name: Dirty Fighting
entries.text: You have been taught all the dirty tricks of unarmed combat. If you make a Called Shot to the body with an unarmed strike and deal any Wounds, you may choose to sacrifice the normal Damage to inflict the Low Blow! Critical Wound (see page 175).

entries.name: Disarm
entries.text: You are able to disarm an opponent with a careful flick of the wrist or a well-aimed blow to the hand. Upon a successful melee strike as the attacker, you may choose to sacrifice the Damage. If you do so, your opponent loses a held weapon, which flies 1d10 feet in a random direction. If you wish, you may lose Momentum to pluck the weapon from the air with a flourish. This Talent is of no use if your opponent fights unarmed, is securely attached to their weapon, or has a larger Size than you (see page 360).

entries.name: Distract
entries.text: You are trained in simple movements to distract or startle your opponent, drawing eyes from your true intent. Upon a successful Melee Attack, you may choose to sacrifice the Damage. If you do so, your opponent loses Momentum and cannot regain it, or make any Test with Advantage for any other reason, until the end of your next Turn.

entries.name: Doomed
entries.text: At the age of 10, you underwent the Dooming, a coming-of-age ritual observed by many humans in the Old World. During the incense-laden rite, a priest of Morr known as a doomsayer foretold the manner of your death. In conjunction with your GM, devise a suitable Doom. If your Character dies in the manner foretold, all allied Characters immediately refresh their Fortune, and your next Character begins play with an additional Fate Point.

entries.name: Drilled
entries.text: You have been trained to fight shoulder-to-shoulder with other soldiers as a single unit. Allies may freely Disengage from an opponent you are also Engaged with as you cover their retreat. Additionally, on your Turn you may lose Momentum in order to grant Momentum to any allies you are standing shoulder to shoulder with, so long as they also have this Talent.

entries.name: Dual Wielder
entries.text: You have a knack for fighting with a weapon in each hand. When fighting with two weapons (see page 167), you do not have to lose Momentum in order to make a free attack with a second weapon. Additionally, when fighting with two weapons, Daggers, Knives, and similar weapons you wield gain the Parry Quality.

entries.name: Embezzle
entries.text: You are skilled at skimming money from your employers without being detected. When Earning during play or performing an Income Endeavour, you can embezzle funds, by using Bribery or Evaluate in place of your normal Earning Skill. If you do this, a successful Test indicates that you have doubled your money. On a failure, irregularities are discovered and you have to spend time and resources covering up your misdeeds: you earn no money whatsoever.

entries.name: Enclosed Fighter
entries.text: You have learned to make the most benefit out of fighting in enclosed spaces. You ignore penalties to Melee Tests caused by confined spaces such as tunnels, the frontline, small fighting pits, and similar. You can also use the Dodge Skill even if it would normally be disallowed due to lack of space.

entries.name: Etiquette (Social Group)
entries.text: You can blend in socially with the chosen group, so long as you are dressed and acting appropriately. Furthermore, the GM may warn your Character if they begin to indulge in behaviour considered inappropriate by the social group. Example social groups include: Criminals, Cultists, Guilders, Nobles, and Soldiers.

entries.name: Fast Hands
entries.text: You can move your hands with surprising dexterity. You can use Sleight of Hand to entertain people by making small objects vanish or appear. You gain Advantage on Sleight of Hand Tests, as well as Melee (Brawling) Tests made to touch an opponent, such as those required by some spells.

entries.name: Fast Shot
entries.text: You can draw and fire a pistol with lightning speed, attacking before the Combat Initiative sequence begins. If you are not Engaged, you may make a single attack with a loaded weapon with the Pistol Trait before the first turn of the Round. This attack uses your Action for the Round. If multiple Characters use Fast Shot, resolve their attacks in Combat Initiative order. When your turn arrives, you act as normal, but cannot make another attack.

entries.name: Fearless (Enemy)
entries.text: You are either brave or crazy enough that fear of certain enemies has become a distant memory. When you take this Talent, choose any enemy group, such as Giants, Skeletons, or Trolls. You are immune to fear from enemies in the chosen group. You may acquire this Talent more than once, choosing a new enemy group each time you do so.

entries.name: Feint
entries.text: You have trained how to make false attacks in close combat to fool your opponent. When attacking in melee, if you have Advantage and your opponent does not, you can force them to defend with Intuition instead of any other Skill or Characteristic.

entries.name: Field Dressing
entries.text: You are used to treating wounds quickly with whatever suitable materials you can find at hand. You make Heal Tests with Advantage, and can easily create basic splints or bandages from ordinary materials.

entries.name: Fisherman
entries.text: You are a very capable fisherman and know all the best ways to land fish. Assuming a large enough body of water is available, and you have the right gear such as a rod or net, you are able to fish enough to feed yourself and a number of others equal to your Initiative Bonus. You may secure more fish in addition to this using the normal rules for foraging (see page 152).

entries.name: Flagellant
entries.text: You have dedicated your pain to the service of your god, and regular and repeated self-inflicted wounds mean that pain now only incites you to greater feats. You feel no pain and may ignore penalties inflicted by Critical Wounds, other than amputations. Additionally, if another ability or effect allows you to Frenzy (page 184), you may enter a Frenzy any time you suffer a Wound without requiring a Test.

entries.name: Flee!
entries.text: When your life is on the line, you are capable of impressive bursts of speed. If you Disengage from combat, you may immediately make an extra Move to sprint away from your opponent. If you choose to Flee in combat (page 163), you do not gain any Broken Conditions. Tests as the Quarry in a Pursuit benefit from +1 SL.

entries.name: Fleet-footed
entries.text: You are unusually fast on your feet, and gain +1 to your Movement Attribute.

entries.name: Frenzy
entries.text: You have a deep well of fury inside you, which you can unleash upon your enemies. Making a successful Willpower Test lets you enter a Frenzy, allowing you to make additional attacks, ignore most psychological effects, and inflict additional Damage in melee. The full rules for Frenzy are described on page 184.

entries.name: Frightening
entries.text: You strike fear into the hearts of your enemies. You gain the Fear Trait with a rating of 1, or 2 if you are Large (see page 360). Enemies must pass an Extended Psychology Test, requiring a number of successes equal to your Fear rating, with one Test made each turn. Until they do, they cannot gain Momentum, and you gain Advantage on Melee Attacks against them.

entries.name: Furious Assault
entries.text: Your blows follow one another in quick succession, raining down on your opponents with the fury of Ulric. Once per Round, if you hit an opponent in melee, you may immediately lose Momentum to make an extra attack.

entries.name: Gregarious
entries.text: You just like talking to other folk, and it seems they like talking to you. You gain Advantage on any Gossip Tests you make, and can usually tell where in a settlement gossip is likely to be exchanged.

entries.name: Gunner
entries.text: You are practised in the use of blackpowder weapons, and are able to lessen some of their more obvious dangers. When using a Blackpowder, Engineering, or Explosive weapon, you ignore the Dangerous Flaw.

entries.name: Hardy
entries.text: When calculating your Wounds total, add your Toughness Bonus an additional time.

entries.name: Hatred (Group)
entries.text: You are consumed with hatred toward your foes. You develop Hatred for a group. When encountering the subject of your Hatred, you must attempt a Psychology Test or immediately attempt to destroy the hated group by the fastest and most deadly means possible. You gain +1 SL on all Melee and Ranged Tests against the specified group, and are immune to Intimidate and Fear (but not Terror) caused by them. Examples you could take include: beastmen, goblins, orcs, monsters, outlaws, Sigmarites, undead, and witches. The full rules for Hatred can be found on page 184.

entries.name: Holy Hatred
entries.text: Your prayers drip with the hatred you feel for your blasphemous enemies. When causing Wounds with a Miracle, you may deal +2 Wounds.

entries.name: Holy Visions
entries.text: You clearly see the great works of the gods all around you. You automatically know when you enter holy ground, can perceive Blessings, Miracles, and Chaos Magic Spells cast within your line of sight, and can sense divine power in an object with a touch.

entries.name: Hunter’s Eye
entries.text: You are a skilled hunter and know all the best techniques to find game. When travelling through well-stocked lands, you are automatically assumed to be able to hunt down enough game to feed yourself and a number of others equal to your Initiative Bonus, so long as you have time and the correct equipment. You may secure more food in addition to this using the normal rules for foraging (see page 152).

entries.name: Impassioned Zeal (Cause)
entries.text: You have a fervent belief in a certain cause, whether it be political, religious, or philosophical. When you talk about your cause, your words fill with passion and fervent zeal. You gain Advantage on Charm Tests when speaking on these matters. You also find it hard to deny, or prevaricate about the cause, and suffer Disadvantage when lying about or denouncing the subject of your passions.

entries.name: Implacable
entries.text: It takes a lot to finish you off. Any time you would gain one or more Bleeding Conditions, you gain one less.

entries.name: In-fighter
entries.text: You are skilled at drawing in close to an opponent and making better use of a shorter weapon. As your Action, you can perform an Opposed Melee Test to attempt to step inside your opponent’s weapon length. The winner chooses if combat continues as normal or as ‘in-fighting’. During in-fighting, any weapon longer than Short counts as an Improvised Weapon. At the start of their Turn, an opponent may choose to lose Momentum in order to end in-fighting.

entries.name: Inspiring
entries.text: Your rousing words and pleas can turn the tide of battle. You have Advantage when you make Leadership Tests in combat.

entries.name: Instinctive Diction
entries.text: You instinctively understand Magick and are capable of articulating complex phrases rapidly and without error. If you are required to roll on the Minor Miscast Table, you may reduce the result by 20. If the final result is less than 01, then no Miscast occurs. If you generate a Major Miscast this Talent has no effect.

entries.name: Invoke (Deity)
entries.text: You are blessed by one of the gods and can empower their cult’s Miracles. Upon learning the Talent, you gain one Miracle of your choice from those available to your patron. You may now memorise additional Miracles from those available to your patron for the following cost in XP. Under normal circumstances, you may not learn more than one Invoke (Deity) Talent. Further, you may not learn the Channelling Skill or the Arcane Magic, Chaos Magic, Magic Resistance, Petty Magic, or Witch! Talents when you have the Invoke Talent, and vice versa. You can unlearn this Talent for 100 XP, but will lose all of your Miracles if you do so, and will garner the extreme disfavour of your god, with effects determined by your GM.

entries.name: Iron Jaw
entries.text: You are made of sturdy stuff and can weather even the strongest blows. The first time in an encounter you would gain one or more Stunned Conditions, you gain one less.

entries.name: Iron Will
entries.text: You possess an indomitable will, and resist willingly bowing down before another. You gain Advantage on Cool Tests made to resist the influence of others, be it through a Fellowship Test or magical means.

entries.name: Jump Up
entries.text: You move with grace and are hard to keep down. You gain Advantage when making a Perform (Acrobatics) Test to entertain or move quickly outside of combat. Whenever you suffer the Prone Condition, you may immediately attempt a Challenging (+0 SL) Athletics or Perform (Acrobatics) Test to spring back to your feet.

entries.name: Kingpin
entries.text: You have earned an air of respectability despite your nefarious ways. The Criminal Talent no longer makes law enforcers suspect you or prevents you from accessing certain Careers. Most other Criminals recognise you as someone to respect — unless they’re well prepared and gunning for your position and status.

entries.name: Lightning Reflexes
entries.text: Gain +5 Agility. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Linguistics
entries.text: You have a natural affinity for languages and learn new ones with ease. You gain Advantage on Language Tests. Additionally, Advances in any Language Specialisations always cost 50 XP, no matter how many Advances you have already taken. This Talent applies only to languages used for true communication — its effects do not apply to Language (Magick).

entries.name: Lip Reading
entries.text: You can work out what people are saying by watching their lips move. If you have an unobstructed view of the speaker’s mouth, you can attempt a Challenging (+0 SL) Intuition Test to understand what they are saying.

entries.name: Luck
entries.text: They say when you were born, Ranald smiled. You gain +1 maximum Fortune. If you wish, you may purchase this Talent up to three times, for a maximum of +3 Fortune.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: You are resistant to magic. The SL of any Spell that would affect you is reduced by 3. Furthermore, if you have this Talent, you may never learn the Channelling Skill or the Arcane Magic, Bless, Chaos Magic, Invoke, Petty Magic, or Witch! Talents, and vice versa.

entries.name: Magical Sense
entries.text: Your senses are especially sharp, and can detect sudden movements and changes in the Winds of Magic, even if you are not a spellcaster. You immediately become aware of any spellcasting within your Perception in yards, although you cannot discern the nature of the magic and can tell only the rough direction of the source. Additionally, if you have the Second Sight Talent, or can otherwise perceive the Winds of Magic, you gain Advantage on any tests made to discern their whims or motions.

entries.name: Magnum Opus
entries.text: You are an undisputed master in your field, able to create works of incredible complexity that inspire awe and envy in your peers. When you take this Talent, you may create a single, extraordinary work of art with one of your Art or Trade Skills. This work is all but unrivalled in your field, a unique piece that will always impress, giving bonuses as determined by the GM, most commonly to Fellowship Tests from those who have witnessed your astounding work. Selling the piece will net you at least ten times its normal value. You may take this Talent multiple times. Each time you do, you create a new masterwork.

entries.name: Marksman
entries.text: Gain +5 Ballistic Skill. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Master of Disguise
entries.text: You are an expert at taking on the appearance and mannerisms of others. With nothing but posture changes, face twisting, and careful use of appropriate clothing, you no longer look like yourself. Furthermore, when you successfully use the Entertain (Acting) Skill, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die.

entries.name: Master Orator
entries.text: You are skilled at speaking on almost any topic, always sounding clear, concise, and confident — even when discussing topics you are unfamiliar with, or taking positions you do not truly believe. You gain Advantage on Lore (Law) Tests made to argue a case before a magistrate, or similar Lore Tests made to argue an academic, theological, or political point before a crowd.

entries.name: Master Tradesman (Trade)
entries.text: You are a skilled and reliable artisan. When you take this Talent, choose a Trade Specialisation. When you successfully use this Skill, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die. You may take this Talent more than once, choosing a new Trade Specialisation each time you do.

entries.name: Menacing
entries.text: You have an imposing presence, and most people know to steer clear of you. You gain Advantage on Intimidation Tests, and most sensible thieves, bandits, and pickpockets will choose another target as long as one is available.

entries.name: Mimic
entries.text: You have a good ear for accents and dialects and can reproduce them accurately. You gain Advantage on Entertain (Acting, Comedy) and Perform (Clowning) Tests. Additionally, you may replicate any accent you are exposed to for at least a day, which may help with dealing with locals in an area at the GM’s discretion. If you are familiar with an accent, you know if another is attempting to fake it or hide it unless they also have Mimic.

entries.name: Night Vision
entries.text: You can see very well in natural darkness. Assuming you have at least a faint source of light (such as moonlight obscured by a Marienburg fog, the glowing eyes of a wight, or a bioluminescent fungus) you can see clearly for 20 yards and can extend the effective illumination distance of any light sources by a further 20 yards.

entries.name: Nimble-fingered
entries.text: Gain +5 Dexterity. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Noble Blood
entries.text: You are either born into the nobility, or otherwise elevated to it by in-game events. Assuming you are dressed appropriately, you are always considered to be at least one Status Tier higher than others unless they also have the Noble Blood Talent, where Status is compared as normal. Furthermore, you may enter the Noble Career as if it were within the same Class as your current Career.

entries.name: Nose for Trouble
entries.text: You are used to getting into, and preferably out of, trouble. You gain Advantage on Intuition Tests, and can usually tell where in a town or village you can find the opportunity to gamble, fight, or get stinking drunk.

entries.name: Numismatics
entries.text: You are well versed with the different coinage of the Old World and are adept at determining the value of artefacts from distant lands. You gain Advantage on Lore (Heraldry) Tests to identify the providence of any coin, medal, or flag. When you successfully make an Evaluate Test to determine the value of an item, you may use either the rolled SL or the value of your units die.

entries.name: Old Salt
entries.text: You are an experienced seaman and are very used to sea life. When you successfully use the Row or Sail Skill on the ocean, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die. You count as two boatmen towards the minimum number of crew to pilot an ocean-going vessel.

entries.name: Orientation
entries.text: You have an instinctive sense of direction. You gain Advantage on Navigation Tests. You also automatically know which direction is north with a glimpse at the stars, trees, or whatever other signs you are familiar with.

entries.name: Panhandle
entries.text: You are a skilled beggar, able to get even the most jaded individual to contribute to your cause. You gain Advantage on Charm Tests while begging, including those made during an Income Endeavour. Additionally, you can usually find the best places to find shelter for a safe but uncomfortable night’s sleep beneath bridges, near middens, and in other urban locations most folks choose to ignore.

entries.name: Perfect Pitch
entries.text: You have perfect pitch, able to replicate notes perfectly. You can learn a piece of music simply by listening to it once, and gain Advantage on Entertain (Singing) and Play (Any) Tests.

entries.name: Petty Magic
entries.text: You have the spark to cast magic within you and have mastered techniques to control it at a basic level. Upon learning the Talent, you manifest a number of Spells equal to your Willpower Bonus. You can learn additional Petty Magic Spells for the following cost in XP. Full rules for learning new Spells are provided in Chapter 8: Magic. You can unlearn this Talent at a cost of 100 XP, but immediately lose all Spells linked to the Talent if you do so. Number of Spells XP Cost for a new Spell currently known Up to 5 50 XP 6 to 10 100 XP 11 to 15 150 XP 16 to 20 200 XP 21 and up 250 XP

entries.name: Pharmacist
entries.text: You are highly skilled at pharmacy, better able than most to make pills, unguents, oils, creams, and more. When creating an alchemical remedy (see page 154), you produce an additional dose.

entries.name: Pilot
entries.text: You are skilled at leading vessels through dangerous waters, high winds, or when making haste to escape pirates or wreckers. Gain Advantage on Row and Sail Tests.

entries.name: Public Speaker
entries.text: You are skilled at rousing crowds of the common folk. You know how to gather a crowd with ease and can usually gauge the mood of a group and what might motivate them to take action. You gain Advantage on Charm Tests made to influence groups of people. Once you have Charmed a group in this way, you may make Leadership Tests to influence them in other ways, urging them to action, removing Broken Conditions, and so on (see page 169).

entries.name: Pure Soul
entries.text: Your soul is pure, quite resistant to the depredations of Chaos. You may gain double the usual number of Corruption Points before having to Test to resist mutation (see page 188).

entries.name: Rapid Reload
entries.text: You reload ranged weapons with practised ease. When using a weapon with the Reload Flaw, reduce the number of the Reload Flaw by 1.

entries.name: Reaction Strike
entries.text: Your fast reactions have allowed you to halt charging enemies in their tracks. When you are Charged, you may attempt a Challenging (+0 SL) Initiative Test to gain an immediate free attack against that charger outside the normal Turn sequence. This attack is resolved with whatever weapon you are carrying in your primary hand. You can only make one free attack this way each round.

entries.name: Read/Write
entries.text: The written word remains a mystery to most denizens of the Empire, but you have learned your letters and can read and write in any language you can speak.

entries.name: Relentless
entries.text: When you have your mind set on a target, there is nothing anyone can do to stop you reaching them. If an opponent Disengages from you, you can attempt a Challenging (+0 SL) Athletics, Drive, or Ride Test after their Turn ends. A success provides an extra Move to chase after them and lets you freely Disengage from all other opponents to do so. Further, any Tests to chase as a Pursuer in a Pursuit benefit from +1 SL.

entries.name: Resistant (Threat)
entries.text: Your strong constitution allows you to more readily survive a specific threat. Once per session, before rolling a Test to resist a specific Threat (such as Disease, Magic, Corruption, Poison), you may choose to automatically pass that Test. You gain Advantage on all further Tests to resist that threat. You may take this Talent more than once, picking a new Threat each time.

entries.name: Resolute
entries.text: You stand firm in the face of danger with grim determination. When you gain a Condition, you may retain your Momentum if you pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Cool Test.

entries.name: Reversal
entries.text: You are used to desperate combats, able to find opportunities to gain an edge in dire circumstances. In an Opposed Melee Test where you are struck but your Test succeeded, you retain Momentum.

entries.name: Riposte
entries.text: Conforming to ‘the best defence is offence’, you respond to an incoming attack with a counterstrike of your own. If you win an Opposed Test when defending in melee combat, you cause Damage as if you were the attacker.

entries.name: River Guide
entries.text: You know all the tricks for navigating dangerous rivers. You need not Test to navigate dangerous waters unless the Difficulty is Difficult (-1 SL) or lower. If you also have the appropriate Lore (Local) Skill, you never need to Test — you are assumed to know a safe route.

entries.name: Robust
entries.text: You are as tough as old boots and quickly recover from injury. Whenever you test to heal Wounds you may heal an additional 2 Wounds.

entries.name: Roughrider
entries.text: You are at home in the saddle in even the most difficult of circumstances and know how to protect your mount from harm during poor conditions. Assuming you have the Ride Skill, you can direct your mount to take an Action, as well as a Move, without a Ride Test. If a Ride Test is required, you may make it with Advantage. Furthermore, when mounted in a Pursuit, add +1 to the animal’s Movement Attribute.

entries.name: Rover
entries.text: You are at home in wild places, moving quickly and quietly through Taal’s own realm. You gain Advantage on Stealth (Rural) Tests, and can usually determine the easiest route through an area, as well as where to find game, water, and shelter.

entries.name: Savant (Lore Specialisation)
entries.text: You are exceptionally learned and have a significant degree of specialised knowledge in your field of study. Choose any Lore Specialisation you possess. Tests made using this Lore Specialisation are made with Advantage. You may acquire this Talent more than once, choosing a new Lore Specialisation each time you do so.

entries.name: Savvy
entries.text: Gain +5 Intelligence. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Scale Sheer Surface
entries.text: You are an exceptional climber. You gain Advantage on Climb Tests. Additionally, you can attempt to climb even seemingly impossible surfaces such as sheer fortifications, ice shelves, greased poles, and similar, at a maximum imposed Difficulty of Very Hard (-3 SL).

entries.name: Schemer
entries.text: You are a master of politics, seeing conspiracy around every corner, and are adept at weaselling secrets and rumour from those in the know. When you successfully use Gossip or Lore (Politics), you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die.

entries.name: Sea Legs
entries.text: You are used to the rolling motion of the oceans, and are unlikely to get seasick, even in the worst storms. Under normal conditions, you need never Test to see if you become seasick, and you gain Advantage on Tests to avoid it should the GM require one.

entries.name: Seasoned Traveller
entries.text: You are an inquisitive soul who has travelled far and wide, and quickly pick up all manner of local information. You can always advance the relevant regional Lore (Local) Skill whilst you remain in that region, even if it is not part of your current Career.

entries.name: Second Sight
entries.text: You can perceive the shifting Winds of Magic that course from the Chaos Gates at the poles of the world. You now have the ability to percieve the Winds of Magic (see page 236).

entries.name: Secret Identity
entries.text: You maintain a secret identity that allows you to appear richer, or perhaps poorer, than you actually are. You can adopt an alternate persona with a Career of your choice for a set period of time (an encounter, a day, an entire adventure) without having to Test to maintain the charade, and during this period you are treated as having the Class and Status of the chosen Career. If you wish, you can even adopt this persona for the purpose of carrying out Banking and Income Endeavours, however, in the case of an Income Endeavour, you must take a Challenging (+0 SL) Earning Test with either Entertain (Acting) or the chosen Career’s normal Earning Skill for the Earning Test (not the Earning Skill of your actual Career). If you have the Embezzle Talent, you can use Bribery or Evaluate instead if you are embezzling. If the Earning Test fails, the ruse is exposed, with consequences determined by the GM.

entries.name: Shadow
entries.text: You are skilled at following people through busy crowds and winding streets without losing your mark. You instinctively know when to abandon a tail before your quarry spots you. If someone you are following succeeds on a Perception Test to spot you, you may either allow them to spot you and continue following them, or lose track of them and remain unseen.

entries.name: Sharp
entries.text: Gain +5 Initiative. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Sharpshooter
entries.text: You can make shots of exceptional accuracy. Ranged Tests you make do not incur any penalties from your target being Prone or in cover. You may also perform feats of accuracy with your weapons that most would think impossible, such as cutting a hangman’s noose with an arrow or punching a hole in a tossed coin with a pistol shot. Such feats of marksmanship still require a successful Ranged Test, with the GM setting the difficulty.

entries.name: Shieldsman
entries.text: You are skilled at using your shield to control the flow of battle. Once per Round, while carrying a shield, you may lose Momentum to either grant your shield’s AP bonus to an adjacent ally who is not carrying a shield, or, if you win an Opposed Melee Test while attacking or defending, push your opponent up to 2 yards directly away and no longer count as Engaged.

entries.name: Sixth Sense
entries.text: You get a strange feeling whenever danger is near. If you are about to trigger a trap or fall victim to a hidden danger, such as an ambush, collapsing tunnel, or poisoned glass of wine, you may make a Challenging (+0 SL) Intuition Test. On a success, you detect the danger at the last possible moment.

entries.name: Slayer
entries.text: You are undaunted by large enemies and attack them with great gusto. If you Charge a creature whose Size is larger than you, you automatically gain Momentum.

entries.name: Small
entries.text: You are much shorter than most folk in the Old World. Gain Size (Small). The full rules for different Sizes are found in Chapter 12: Bestiary on page 360.

entries.name: Sniper
entries.text: Distance is of no import to your shooting skills, and you are just as adept at picking off far away targets as those nearby. You suffer no penalties for shooting at Long Range, and only a -1 SL penalty for shots made at Extreme Range.

entries.name: Speedreader
entries.text: You read books at a voracious pace. A single glance is all you require to read a full page of text, and you can easily make your way through even a lengthy tome in a single day. When you make an Extended Research Test, double the SL added by any successful Test you make.

entries.name: Sprinter
entries.text: You are a swift runner with a good level of physical fitness. You gain Advantage on Athletics Tests to run and jump.

entries.name: Step Aside
entries.text: You are skilled at being where enemy weapons are not. If you successfully use Dodge to defend against an attack, you may move up to 2 yards as you dive away, and no longer count as Engaged. Opponents do not gain a free attack when you do this.

entries.name: Stone Soup
entries.text: You are used to getting by with less, and know how to survive lean times. If a member of the party makes a Foraging Test (see page 152), they automatically locate sufficient food to feed you, over and above the number of Characters fed by the Test result, even if the Test fails.

entries.name: Stout-hearted
entries.text: No matter how bad things get, you always seem to come back for more. The first time in an encounter you gain one or more Broken Conditions, you gain one less.

entries.name: Striding Gait (Terrain)
entries.text: You are experienced in traversing difficult ground. You ignore all movement penalties when crossing over or through a specified terrain. If engaged in a Pursuit in your chosen terrain, you receive +2 SL to all Tests relating to the Pursuit. Example Terrains are: Coastal, Desert, Rocky, Tundra, Wetland, Woodland. You may take this Talent more than once, choosing a new Terrain each time you do.

entries.name: Strike Mighty Blow
entries.text: You know how to hit hard! You inflict +1 extra Damage with melee weapons, or +2 if your attack was made with Advantage.

entries.name: Strike to Injure
entries.text: You are an expert at striking your enemies’ most vulnerable areas. When rolling on a Critical Wound table, roll twice and choose which result you prefer. Further, you ignore the Called Shot penalty when going for a Silent Takedown (see page 135).

entries.name: Strike to Stun
entries.text: You know how to use your weapon to subdue, not kill. You count all Improvised Weapons as having the Pummel Quality. When using a Pummel weapon, ignore the Called Shot penalty when going for a Silent Takedown (see page 135).

entries.name: Strong Back
entries.text: You have a strong back that is used to hard work. You gain a bonus of +1 SL to any Opposed Strength Test, and the amount of Encumbrance you can carry increases by one. If you wish, you may purchase this Talent a second time, increasing the bonus to +3 SL and the number of additional Encumbrance points to three.

entries.name: Strong Legs
entries.text: You have strong legs able to carry you great distances when you jump. When you successfully use the Athletics Skill to sprint or leap, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die.

entries.name: Strong-minded
entries.text: You are the epitome of determination and resolve. Once per session, before taking a Test, you may choose to take that Test without any negative modifiers.

entries.name: Strong Swimmer
entries.text: You are an accomplished swimmer, able to fight a strong current and outpace other swimmers. You gain Advantage on Swim Tests, and receive a +2 SL Bonus to swimming Pursuits.

entries.name: Sturdy
entries.text: You have a brawny physique, or are very used to carrying things. When calculating the number of Encumbrance Points you can carry, count your Strength Bonus twice.

entries.name: Suave
entries.text: Gain +5 Fellowship. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Super Numerate
entries.text: You have a gift for calculation and can work out solutions to most mathematical problems with ease, without the need for a quill, paper, or abacus. You gain Advantage on Evaluate Tests, and you can keep track of the passage of time accurately so long as you are conscious.

entries.name: Supportive
entries.text: You know what to say and when to make the most impact upon your superiors. You not only ignore the penalty to using Charm on those of a higher Status Tier, but also gain Advantage on Charm Tests made to ingratiate yourself with those of higher Status.

entries.name: Sure Shot
entries.text: You are skilled in placing your shots exactly where they will do the most damage, tearing through vital organs and finding vulnerabilities in your target’s armour. Your Ranged Attacks inflict +1 Damage, and may ignore armour with the Partial Flaw. If your weapon has the Impale Quality, you can ignore armour with the Weakpoints Flaw as well.

entries.name: Surgery
entries.text: You are a surgeon, able to open and close the flesh in order to heal others. When you successfully use the Heal Skill outside of combat, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die. Furthermore, you can treat any Critical Wound marked as needing Surgery, for effects see pages 172 to 179.

entries.name: Tenacious
entries.text: You are a vigorous sort. The first time in an encounter you would gain one or more Fatigued Conditions, you gain one less.

entries.name: Tinker
entries.text: You are somewhat of a Johann-of-all-trades, able to repair almost anything. You count all Trade Skills as Basic when repairing broken items. If you have at least 1 Advance in a Trade Skill, you have Advantage on Tests to repair associated items, and such repairs take half as much time.

entries.name: Tower of Memories
entries.text: A recollection technique first instigated by the Cult of Verena, reputedly from elven practices taught by the loremasters of Hoeth, Tower of Memories allows you to perfectly recall a significant amount of facts by storing them in an imaginary spire. When you successfully use the Lore Skill, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die.

entries.name: Trapper
entries.text: You are skilled at using all manner of traps, and know how to make basic snares and pitfalls from whatever comes to hand. You gain Advantage on Set Trap Tests. Additionally, with an hour to prepare, you can craft a small animal trap or covered pit (see page 136).

entries.name: Trick Rider
entries.text: You are capable of amazing feats of agility while in the saddle. You can use any of your Perform Skills and unmodified Dodge Skill when mounted.

entries.name: Tunnel Fighter
entries.text: You are at home in tunnels, sewers, and other underground environments. You gain Advantage on Stealth (Underground) Tests, and can easily tell how far you have travelled underground and roughly how deep beneath the surface you are.

entries.name: Unshakeable
entries.text: You are a jaded veteran who has survived more than one hail of shots from blackpowder weapons. You do not need to Test to resist a Broken Condition if shot at by a Blackpowder weapon.

entries.name: Very Resilient
entries.text: Gain +5 Toughness. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: Very Strong
entries.text: Gain +5 Strength. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: War Leader
entries.text: Your stern gaze and inspiring words motivate your soldiers to fight on to the end. All allies you influence with Leadership during battle (see page 169) may use your Leadership rather than their Cool to resist Fear until the end of the battle. The effect ends if you die, or while you are subject to Broken, Unconscious, or Fear Conditions.

entries.name: Warrior Born
entries.text: Gain +5 Weapon Skill. This does not count toward Advances.

entries.name: War Wizard
entries.text: You are trained to cast magic while in the thick of combat. On your Turn, you may cast one Spell with a Casting Number of 5 or less for free without using your Action. If you do this, you may not cast another Spell this Turn.

entries.name: Waterman
entries.text: You are an experienced freshwater sailor and are well-versed with river vessels. When you successfully use the Row or Sail Skill on a river or lake, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die. You count as two crewmen towards the minimum number of crew to pilot a river vessel.

entries.name: Wealthy
entries.text: You are fabulously wealthy and are rarely ever short of coin. For the purpose of securing money through your Career, either during play or performing an Income Endeavour, you obtain 1 additional gold crown. You may take this Talent a second time, allowing you to secure 3 additional gold crowns instead.

entries.name: Well-prepared
entries.text: You are used to anticipating the needs of others, and yourself. Once per session, you may pull a Trapping required for the current situation from your pockets, as long as it is Encumbrance 0, could feasibly have been bought recently, and does not stretch credulity too far. You can use this Talent more times in the same session by spending Fortune. Whenever you use this ability, you must deduct the cost for the item, representing money you spent earlier. If you have no money, you may not use this Talent.

entries.name: Witch!
entries.text: You have learned magic through trial and error. Gain one Spell of your choice from any Colour Lore or the Lore of Witchcraft, even if you lack the appropriate Arcane Magic Talent. Further, treat that Spell’s Channelling Skill as a Basic Skill. You can memorise an additional such Spell (and treat its Channelling Skill as Basic) for 150 XP; further Spells cost 50 XP more each time. Possession of this Talent may attract the attention of witch hunters, and complicate matters should you wish to join an established magical tradition. You can spend 100 XP to lose this Talent and all associated Spells.

entries.name: Blessing of Battle
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Weapon Skill.

entries.name: Blessing of Breath
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target does not need to breathe and ignores rules for Suffocation.

entries.name: Blessing of Charisma
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Fellowship.

entries.name: Blessing of Conscience
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target must pass an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test to break any of the strictures of your deity. If they fail, they are overcome with shame and do not take the action.

entries.name: Blessing of Courage
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Willpower.

entries.name: Blessing of Finesse
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Dexterity.

entries.name: Blessing of Fortune
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target may reroll their next failed Test. The reroll must stand.

entries.name: Blessing of Grace
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Agility.

entries.name: Blessing of Hardiness
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Toughness.

entries.name: Blessing of Healing
entries.text: Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Instant Your target heals +1 Wound.

entries.name: Blessing of The Hunt
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Ballistic Skill.

entries.name: Blessing of Might
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Strength.

entries.name: Blessing of Protection
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Enemies must make an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test to attack your target as shame wells within for considering violence. If they fail, they must choose a different target, or a different Action.

entries.name: Blessing of Recuperation
entries.text: Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Instant Your target may reduce the duration of 1 disease with which they are afflicted by 1 day. This prayer may only be attempted once per instance of a disease per person.

entries.name: Blessing of Righteousness
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target’s weapon counts as Magical.

entries.name: Blessing of Savagery
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds When your target next inflicts a Critical Wound, roll twice and choose the best result.

entries.name: Blessing of Tenacity
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: Instant Your target may remove 1 Condition (except Besmirched).

entries.name: Blessing of Wisdom
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Intelligence.

entries.name: Blessing of Wit
entries.text: Range: 6 yards Target: 1 Duration: 6 rounds Your target gains +10 Initiative. BLESSING NAMES Each cult has unique names for every Blessing — sometimes more than one name. For instance, the Cult of Sigmar may refer to the Blessing of Battle as The Litany of Sigmar’s Wrath, while the Cult of Ulric may call it The Sharp Bite of Winter. The words spoken will be different, but the end effect will be the same.

entries.name: Becalm
entries.text: Range: Fellowship Bonus miles Target: 1 sailing vessel within line of sight Duration: 1 hour You steal the wind from the sails of a ship or boat. It is completely becalmed. Even in stormy weather, an area of eerie calm and smooth waters surrounds the vessel while gales, lashing rains and towering crests surge and crash around it. This area of calm extends for Fellowship yards from the vessel, and if the ship is propelled by some other method, such as oars, the area of calm travels with it.
entries.target: 1 sailing vessel within line of sight

entries.name: Drowned Man’s Face
entries.text: Range: Fellowship yards Target: 1 Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds You implore Manann to drown your foe. Your target’s lungs continuously fill with saltwater while the Miracle is active, and their hair floats around their head as if submerged. For the duration, the target suffers a Fatigued Condition and drowns (see page 169). The water is holy, so daemons and undead drown too. When the Miracle ends, your target suffers a Stunned Condition for 1 Round as they cough out seawater.

entries.name: Fair Winds
entries.text: Range: Initiative Bonus miles Target: 1 sailing vessel within line of sight Duration: 1 hour The target vessel’s sails fill with favourable winds, speeding them safely towards their destination. While this Miracle is active, the sailing vessel moves at top speed, no matter the prevailing wind, tide, or current, and all Sail Tests made to control the vessel gain a bonus of +1 SL.
entries.target: 1 sailing vessel within line of sight

entries.name: Manalt’s Bounty
entries.text: Range: Special Target: Special Duration: Instant You implore the Lord of Sea’s Bounty to provide you with sustenance. Reaching into a body of water, you catch enough fish to feed 1 person. If you reach into the sea, you provide enough fish for 2 people. For every +2 SL, you may feed another person.

entries.name: Sea Legs
entries.text: Range: Fellowship yards Target: 1 Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds Your target is immediately drenched in saltwater, and reels as if on the rolling deck of a tempest-tossed vessel. Their hair is whipped by spectral winds, and a torrent of spray lashes their skin. They gain one each of the Blinded, Deafened, and Fatigued Conditions, and must attempt an Average (+2 SL) Athletics Test to use their Move. If they fail, they also gain the Prone Condition.

entries.name: Waterwalk
entries.text: Range: You Target: You Duration: Fellowship Bonus minutes You call on Manann to allow you to cross a stretch of open water as if it were solid ground. This only works on larger bodies of water that are at least 10 yards wide. Anything smaller is too far removed from Manann’s domain for it to be noticed.

entries.name: Death Mask
entries.text: Range: You Target: You Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds Morr works through you, piercing the Portal to make his presence known to your foes. Your visage takes on a cadaverous mien, and you gain Fear. Undead are not immune to this Fear regardless of any Talents, Traits (including Construct), or other effects.

entries.name: Destroy Undead
entries.text: Range: Yo Target: AoE (Fellowship Bonus yards) Duration: Instant You call the power of Morr to smite all undead. A black fire ripples forth from your body in a perfect circle. All targets with the Undead Creature Trait lose 1d10 Wounds, ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Any undead destroyed by this Miracle can never be raised with Necromancy again under normal conditions. For every SL, you may cause 1 additional Wound.

entries.name: Dooming
entries.text: Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Instant Gazing deeply into your target’s eyes while muttering a threnody to Morr, you are granted a vision of the target’s Doom, a glimpse of what the future holds. This is almost always related to the target’s death. This Miracle may only be performed on a character once, after which the Doomed Talent may be purchased with XP as if it were in the target’s Career.

entries.name: Last Rites
entries.text: Range: 1 yard Target: 1 Duration: Instant You chant a solemn requiem over a corpse. This Miracle ensures that the soul is sent through the portal to Morr’s realm, and guarantees the cadaver may not be targeted by any Necromantic spells. If the Miracle targets a foe with the Construct and Undead Creature Traits, it will be destroyed.

entries.name: Portal’s Threshold
entries.text: Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Until sunrise You draw a line up to 8 yards long on the ground while incanting a dirge to Morr. Upon enacting the Miracle, an indistinct, shadowy portal seems to manifest to the hoarse croaking of ravens. Creatures with the Undead Creature Trait must pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Cool Test to cross the line. Creatures with both Undead and Construct simply cannot cross the line.

entries.name: Stay Morr’s Hand
entries.text: Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Fellowship Bonus hours You touch the eyes of someone close to death and request Morr guide the soul within, but not take it. The target must have 0 Wounds and be willing. For the duration of the Miracle, the target gains the Unconscious Condition and will not deteriorate until the Miracle ends, staving off disease, ignoring Critical Wounds and poisons, and similar. This Miracle comes to an end should appropriate healing be provided, or should you perform the last rites. If you do this, which takes about a minute, the target’s soul will pass through Morr’s portal upon death, and the resulting corpse may never be targeted by Necromancy.

entries.name: Blazing Sun
entries.text: Range: Special Target: Special Duration: Instant You call on Myrmidia to scour the battlefield of dishonourable foes, and a blinding flash of golden light bursts forth. All non-Myrmidians looking in your direction receive 1 Blinded Condition. For every +2 SL, they receive +1 Blinded Condition.

entries.name: Eagle’s Eye
entries.text: Range: Fellowship yards Target: You Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds You call on Myrmidia to send a Divine Servant to grant you knowledge of your enemies. A spectral eagle manifests, soaring into the sky above. The eagle looks like and has the capabilities of a normal eagle, but cannot physically affect the world or be harmed in any way. While the Miracle is in effect, you can see through the eagle’s eyes and control its flight, surveying the battlefield and spying upon your enemies. The eagle has Perception 55, Acute Sense (Sight), and Fly 80; you see using its abilities instead of your own. While looking through the eagle’s eyes, you cannot see through your own eyes, leaving you potentially vulnerable.

entries.name: Fury’s Call
entries.text: Range: You Target: AoE (Fellowship Bonus yards) Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds Your passionate prayers instil your allies with a furious disdain for their foes. Allied characters receive the Frenzy Creature Trait (see page 358).

entries.name: Inspiring
entries.text: Range: You Target: AoE (Fellowship Bonus yards) Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds Your rousing prayers inspire discipline and coordination within the ranks. Allied characters gain +1 Drilled Talent.

entries.name: Shield of Myrmidia
entries.text: Range: Fellowship yards Target: Fellowship Bonus Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds Your stalwart prayers incite Myrmidia to shield your allies in glittering, gossamer strands of light, warding enemy blows. Allies gain +1 Armour Point on all Hit Locations.

entries.name: Spear of Myrmidia
entries.text: Range: You Target: You Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds If wielding a spear, it gains the Impact Quality and counts as Magical.

entries.name: An Invitation
entries.text: Range: 1 yard Target: 1 Duration: Instant You spin one of Ranald’s riddles concerning portals, and whether they exist if closed. A door, window, or hatch you target has one method of securing it undone — a lock unlocks, a latch unlatches, a rope unties. For every +2 SL, you may target another method of securing the door, window, or hatch.

entries.name: Cat’s Eyes
entries.text: Range: Fellowship yards Target: You Duration: Fellowship Bonus Rounds Does anything exist that cannot be seen? You riddle with Ranald, who sends a Divine Servant in the form of a cat as an answer. The cat has the capabilities of a normal cat, but cannot be harmed in any way. While the Miracle is in effect, you perceive everything the cat perceives and control its movement. Your senses are as sharp as a cat’s, but you do not have access to any of your own sense-enhancing Talents such as Night Vision. While the Miracle is in effect, you cannot perceive anything through your own senses, leaving you vulnerable.

entries.name: Cheat the Odds
