Barak Varr’s ships are equipped to fight at range and up close. The guns of all ships except the gunboat are mounted in sealed turrets to protect the gun crews, while hydraulic mechanisms powered by the ship’s steam plant allows the turret to rotate as needed. This lets the ship swiftly bring its guns to bear on an enemy, rather than turn the entire hull.

Like their land-bound cousins, the Dwarfs of Barak Varr like to get up close and personal in a fight. All Dwarf ships other than the gunboat are equipped with steel rams meant to punch holes in the enemy’s wooden hulls, the Dwarf ship pulling back and striking again and again until the enemy sinks. Few captains have the courage — or are sufficiently insane — to face an oncoming Ironclad as its steamwhistle bellows a challenge.

Rams play a role in boarding actions, too. When a captain decides it is better to capture a ship as a prize than sink it, he rams it once to hold it in place. Then the crew swing a hydraulic ramp into place, across which a squad of axe and hammer-wielding Dwarfs charge to seize the other vessel. Many see it as proof that Dwarfs who go to sea are ‘not quite right in the head’, because they charge in full armour — over the open ocean!

Dwarf Watercraft are piloted with the Sail Skill. Each Watercraft has its own Specialisation, but a Character with Advances in any Sail Specialisation treats all other Sail Specialisations as Basic Skills. Critical hits against boats might inflict penalties to Sail Tests, deal 9 Damage to occupants due to flying splinters, or even cause the boat to take on water.

entries.name: Gunboat
entries.text:
Vital to their trade with Karaz-a-Karak and the rest of Karaz Ankor beyond it, the Dwarfs of Barak Varr fought hard to secure the route for its trade barges. Under threat from greenskins and Trolls, as well as less-than- neighbourly petty rulers among the Border Princes, the Dwarfkings found themselves forced to devote large numbers of warriors to protect the barges, both coming and going. Even then, losses could be heavy.

Tasked by the Dwarfking to ‘do something’, in the 19th century IC the Engineers of Barak Varr came up with the ‘Gunboat’. An armour-clad, steam-driven ship the size of an Imperial patrol boat, about 25 feet long, the gunboat mounts its engine amidships for greater efficiency as it drives twin paddlewheels, one on each side. Gunboats usually carry a crew of eight — a captain, a pilot and his relief, four gunners, and an engineer to maintain the engine — but can carry up to a half-dozen more Dwarfs, if the threats warrant it. Regardless of crew numbers, all Dwarfs on a gunboat are trained warriors, ready to fight in addition to their other duties. To provide shelter at night, Barak Varr maintains a variety of fortified inn, the walls of which also provide protection to docked rivercraft, about a day’s travel from each other. Surrounded by often-hostile country, visitors other than Dwarfs are a rare sight.

On escort duty or patrol, gunboats frequently travel in pairs for mutual support. Protecting a convoy, one will lead a group of barges, while the other brings up the rear, both on constant watch for ambushes. If on patrol and the need arises to check something onshore, one boat will stay on watch, while the crew of the other investigates. Barak Varr often sends small patrols such as these up the tributaries of the Skull and Blood rivers to make sure no threats are building in the ‘backcountry’.

Gunboats mount a ram on the prow, which provides 5 Armour Points, and can be used to effectively neutralise boats of similar size by smashing into them. All other parts of the Gunboat have 2 Armour Points of protection.

Each Gunboat mounts two turrets, which can be a Swivel Gun or Volley Gun. The forward gun rests in a ‘gun pit’ with a 180 degree firing arc, which provides hard cover to the crew (a –30 hit modifier on ranged attacks). The rear gun is on a raised platform with a 360 firing arc, providing medium cover (a –20 modifier on ranged attacks).

entries.name: Steam Barge
entries.text:
Prior to the steam engine, barges travelling between Karaz Ankor and the Karaz-a-Karak road had to be towed upstream by mule teams, or even by gangs of Dawi pulling on tow ropes. This made the trips even more dangerous and costly, as the craft and their crews were vulnerable to attack. In times of turmoil, losses could be high, and the risk was always present that Barak Varr could be cut off from Karaz Ankor.

Along with the gunboat, then, the hold’s Engineers developed a steam-powered barge that allowed each barge to be manned by fewer crew and travel in the middle of the river, farther from dangerous shores. Propelled by a single paddlewheel at the rear, the steam barge is a flat platform 30 feet in length and 10 feet wide, with low walls around the deck. The deck supports two small cabins, one at the rear for the engine and paddlewheel mechanism, the other in the middle for the crew. The usual crew consists of a captain, the Engineer, and two labourer Dwarfs. A reversed tiller at the bow controls two rudders used for steering.

Other than the cabins, the deck is open for the carrying of cargo. When not powering the wheel, the steam engine is used to operate a collapsible crane for loading and unloading cargo in nets. With careful loading, the capacity of a steam barge is much greater than that of a large Imperial river barge, 800 Enc.

Unarmoured, slow, and with only personal weapons for the crew, the steam barge is not made for combat. Instead, travelling in convoys of up to five barges, it relies on the protection of the escorting gunboats during the day and the fortified inns at night.

entries.name: Dreadnought
entries.text:
The Dreadnought is the latest evolution of Barak Varr’s surface ships, an immense warship capable of sinking an entire enemy flotilla on its own. With the farthest range of any Dwarf warship as well as awesome size and armament, the Kings of Barak Varr have often chosen the Dreadnought to ‘show the colours’ in other lands, whenever necessary to impress — or intimidate — outsiders.

Three great paddlewheels, one on each side and a larger one at the stern, propel the Dreadnoughts the length of the Black Gulf and far out into the Southern Sea. A great engine room, more complex and powerful than any yet designed by Barak Varr’s naval workshops, powers the wheels and the ships turrets and steering system. More heavily armed than any previous class of Dwarf ship, there are two turrets each fore and aft, one in each pair mounted above and behind the other. Each turret mounts a pair of Thunder cannon — a salvo from these is so powerful, it would roll or tear apart any ship less massive than a Dreadnought. Two smaller turrets higher up toward the bridge each support a single Tempest cannon, while five Breaker cannons on each side add to a broadside. Rounding out its armaments, like Ironclads, the Dreadnought has small ports used for anti-personnel fire against enemy ships.

Dreadnoughts have 2 Armour Points of protection to all locations. At the fore and aft, two turrets bear two Thunder Cannons each, for eight Thunder Cannons in total. Each pair of turrets is positioned so that one is above and behind the other. Towards the bridge, two higher, smaller turrets bear a Tempest Cannon each, and five Breaker Cannons on each side provide a broadside. Like Ironclads, Dreadnoughts have small ports used for anti-personnel fire against enemy ships.

Alternate weapon configurations are common, to suit the preferences of the Engineer who crafted it, and the Admiral in command. For example, Grudgebreaker-class battleships mount only one turret of three Thunder Cannons, to make space for the launch pad of a small combat dirigible.

entries.name: Ironclad
entries.text:
Larger, more stable, and more heavily armed and armoured than a Monitor, the Ironclad is the mainstay of Barak Varr’s fleet, able to project power far out to sea or other lands.

Dual paddlewheels, one on each side and each powered by its own engine, provide the Ironclad with after turns and much more manoeuvrability overall than not only a Monitor, but the ships of other species and nations. Crewed by 75 to 100 Dwarfs, Ironclads have two enclosed turrets, fore and aft. Each mount a battery of two Tempest cannons, while above and behind each of these is a secondary battery of one Breaker, each. Casements on each side provide space for a further four Breakers, each.

Ironclads also have many small gun ports on each side for use during boarding actions, when the covering hatches are dropped and crew-dwarfs can sweep the enemy decks with swivel guns, volley guns, or even crossbows.

Ironclads have 2 Armour Points of protection to all locations, with enclosed turrets to the fore and aft. Each mounts a battery of two Tempest Cannons, with a Breaker Cannon above and behind each turret. Casements provide space for a further four Breaker Cannons on each side. Ironclads also have many small gun ports on each side for use during boarding actions, when the covering hatches are dropped and crew can sweep the enemy decks with swivel guns, volley guns, or crossbows.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.text:
Monitors were the firsts ships designed at Barak Varr, and were a response to the threat of pirates and other raiders to coastal shipping. They operate in and just beyond the Blood River delta and guard the approaches to Barak Varr, as well as the coasts as far west as the River Treblecz and the allied manling port of Somjek, and as far south as a day’s sailing from the hold.

The steel hull sits low in the water, supporting a squat, enclosed top castle affectionately referred to as the ‘turtle’. From this arises both the funnel for the steam engine, which powers a single rear paddlewheel, and a gunnery turret that can rotate through a 270 degrees arc, its only ‘blind spot’ being where the funnel sits behind it.

Crewed by 20-25 Dwarfs, Monitors are capable of attacking at range and by ramming. The turret mounts two cannon, usually Breakers, but some are field testing switching one for a flame cannon for use against wooden ships. Beyond the turret guns, Monitors are armed with up to five Breaker cannons on each side, for a formidable broadside.

Their low freeboard limits their seaworthiness, however, as rough weather can swamp them. Monitors thus mainly serve a coastal defence role. To project power further out to sea, Barak Varr developed the Ironclad. Monitors are fitted with a ram, a turret, and 2 Armour Points of protection (as Gunboats). The turret usually mounts two Breaker Cannons, but replacing one with a Flame Cannon is a popular choice for use against wooden ships. Beyond the turret guns, Monitors are armed with up to five Breaker cannons on each side, for a formidable broadside.

entries.name: Nautilus Submersible
entries.text:
The oddest class of ship in Barak Varr’s fleet, the Nautilus steam submersible is capable of travelling both on and below the surface of the water. When on the surface, it resembles nothing so much as a Monitor, but with two turrets, one fore and aft, each housing a single Breaker cannon. Instead of a ram, two torpedo tubes are mounted in the bow. The only ship not to use paddlewheels, submersibles move by means of dual screws.

The Nautilus’s most notable feature is its ability to submerge under the waves, travel underwater, and stay there for extended periods of time. When the captain gives the order, the crew seals the hatches tight, opens a set of valves and floods the ballast tanks in the hull. With a trained crew, a submersible can vanish beneath the waves in less than a minute. To surface, air from compressed tanks is forced into the ballast tanks, pushing the water out.

Nautilus Submersibles are armed with two Breaker Cannon turrets (fore and aft), with two Nautilus Torpedoes ready to fire from a pair of tubes mounted in the bow.

The Nautilus can safely dive to a depth of 30 yards, and stay there for up to one hour. Whilst underwater, it reduces its Move to 2, and cannot fire its Breaker Cannons. However, it may still fire its Nautilus Torpedoes, and is effectively immune to enemy fire — unless the enemy has a means to launch underwater attacks, or can force the submersible to resurface.

After one hour, the effects of oxygen depletion and boiler fumes begin to suffocate the Nautilus’ crew (WFRP Core Rulebook), unless the vessel resurfaces for at least three hours. Consequently, Nautilus captains prefer to travel on the surface, diving only when absolutely necessary.

A Nautilus Submersible can push itself to greater depths of 30 yards, but doing so places extraordinary pressure upon the vessel’s hull. The Nautilus makes a Challenging (+0) Toughness Test every 10 minutes or so it spends at lower depths, with increased difficulties for extreme depths. If the Test is failed, the vehicle suffers 30 Wounds from springing leaks and the buckling hull. A trained crew can make Sail (Nautilus) and Trade (Engineer) Tests to anticipate the submersible’s limits, safely resurfacing before Toughness Tests become necessary.

Submersibles normally have a crew complement of 20, but finding sufficient crew can sometimes be difficult. While the Dwarfs of Barak Varr can overcome the traditional Dawi aversion to not being on or under land, the idea of going under the water is too much for most. The assumption is that a Dwarf must be somewhat unhinged to actually want to do this.

But there are Dwarfs daring and even reckless enough to do this. Joining a Nautilus crew, where casualties can be high, is for some an alternative to expiating shame by taking the Slayer’s oath. Indeed, the King of Barak Varr has formally offered the choice of submersible service, instead of becoming a Slayer, a proposition that has been learned of and taken up by others of distant holds.

entries.name: Torpedo
entries.text:
Price Enc Availability

Range 500 100 Exotic 1,000 Torpedoes have a reputation for being somewhat unreliable. While a failed Challenging (+0) Ranged (Engineering) Test indicates a simple miss, and failure that is also a double requires a roll on the Torpedo Misfire Table.

entries.name: Torpedo Misfires
entries.text:
| D100 | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 01-45 | The clockwork engine stalls, and the torpedo fails to fire. Another attempt is possible in 1d3 rounds. |
| 46-85 | The warhead is a dud. |
| 86-00 | Catastrophe! The torpedo becomes stuck in the tube, but the timer on the explosive is running. The crew have 2d3 rounds to either eject the torpedo or stop the timer before it explodes. |

lot of muffled shouting that climaxed in the King and the Captain exchanging heated accusations.

At that and without a further word, Captain Nihmok stalked out of the throne room, never to be seen in Barak Varr again. The next morning, harbour workers discovered his latest Nautilus, the Hammer of the Sea was gone, as was its crew and Nihmok himself. After weeks of no word, rumour reached Barak Varr of a renegade Nautilus attacking ships from the Black Gulf to the coast of Bretonnia. It was the Hammer.

The pattern of his targets made no sense. He would strike Sartosan pirates, the ships of the Dark Elves, even Marienburg merchantmen. And yet, at least in the case of Human crews, he would rescue survivors and set them ashore, before vanishing back under the waves. And, just as strange, the reports said he refused to ever again set foot on land.

No one knows why Captain Nihmok does this, nor where his secret base is and how he replenishes his supplies. But several nations have proclaimed large rewards for his capture or death. Strangely, King Zamnil is not one of them.

entries.name: Barrakul
entries.text:
Barrakul, translated as ‘Hope of the Mountains’, is a Runic Longsword crafted by an unknown Runesmith and historically wielded by the one-eyed Daemon Slayer Harbek Armgusson, and by the Human Templar Siegfried von Kesselring.

A shining longsword, sheathed in a gem-encrusted leather scabbard with finely inlaid metalwork, the runes of the weapon glow ruby, etched down the blade. When drawn and used in combat, it is said that the blade flows through visibility, at first sight a sharp and clean blade, then an empty space the next, leaving only the floating red runes below the hilt, before reappearing the other side of its victim. The sword is also said to be able to bypass any non-magical protection, phasing through shields and armour alike.

The weapon was originally taken from the corpse of an Orc whose Warband was found desecrating a temple to the Ancestor Gods, slain by Harbek and his band. Though an initial investigation into the blade provided no answers as to its origins, no extensive effort was made to further research the blade’s creation, for fear of being honour bound to return the weapon.

The ultimate fate of the Slayer, whether he achieved his oath of dying in glorious combat, or lost his life in any number of potentially lethal adventuring exploits, is unknown. What is known is that after his passing, the sword was given into the possession of one of his travelling companions, a rare Dwarven Priest of the Cult of Sigmar. It is believed that the weapon was then passed down, through the cult, until it was wielded by Siegfried von Kesselring.

Siegfried, a Templar and loyal servant of Sigmar, was visiting a newly constructed temple in Wittgendorf when the town came under attack by a Beastman horde, led by a Warrior of Chaos. After seeing to the evacuation of the citizens and leading what defence he could, he was forced to fall back to the temple, where he swore an oath to allow not one enemy inside.

Von Kesselring is said to have fought on the steps for a number of hours. Filled with a righteous fury and with an uplifting zeal, he slew countless foes, including the Chaos Marauder, and was able to maintain his defence until reinforcements from a nearby town arrived to help, but he would ultimately succumb to his wounds. He was honoured and interred within the temple’s crypt bearing Barrakul, in a funeral conducted by the Grand Theogonist himself. Many hundreds of years later, the crypt would be investigated and Von Kesselring’s tomb opened. His body had decayed to bones and his armour rusted away, but Barrakul sat pristine and sparkling upon his corpse.

entries.name: Ghal Maraz
entries.text:
Ghal Maraz, known as the ‘Hammer of Sigmar’ to Humans or ‘Skull-Splitter’ in the Dwarfen tongue, is the magical warhammer famously brandished by Sigmar Heldenhammer himself.

Creation of the hammer is attributed to the venerated Ancestor God Smednir, at the dawn of time. Even the most masterfully crafted weapon cannot contain the power of more than three runes, but such is the power of Ghal Maraz that, depending on what source you listen to, it is believed to house as many as five.

Gifted to Prince Sigmar as thanks when he and his Unberogen warriors assisted in the rescue of the Dwarf High King Kurgan Ironbeard from the Orc Warlord Vagraz Headstomper and his force of Greenskins, and as a symbol of the friendship long shared between Dwarf and the Unberogen tribe of Men. When Sigmar felt his years coming to a close, he abdicated his throne and endeavoured to return the hammer to the High King of Karaz Ankor that had gifted it to him, only for he and the hammer to disappear when he entered the Black Fire Pass.

In 500 I.C, an Imperial Dwarf delegation would return the hammer to Emperor Sigismund II. To hear them tell it, a human had brought the hammer to Karaz-a-Karak a few years after Sigmar disappeared, presenting it to the High King and leaving without giving his name. They claimed that the hammer remained among the heirlooms of the clan, until the High King was visited by Grungni in a dream where he bade him return the hammer to the humans, as a time was coming when they would need it.

Most notably, it is of contested historical record whether this hammer wielded by Emperor Sigismund II and the subsequent Emperors up until Karl Franz is the Ghal Maraz of legend. This is referred to as the “Two Hammer Theory” by those that would find themselves on the

While the Cult of Sigmar and the Imperial government both state that the hammer wielded by Karl Franz is the original hammer given to Sigmar in his time before his ascension, it is argued that the powers that the hammer should grant its user appear not to match those told in tales of old, though dismissed as a simple fact of fanciful retellings according to Imperial Scholars.

The truth of the matter is that the hammer handed down through the succession of Emperors was in fact a masterfully crafted duplicate, blessed by Sigmarite Priests and crafted by expert Runesmiths, granting those that held it increased strength, renewing their vitality and allowing their attacks to bypass non-magical armour.

Following an encounter between adventurers and the Tzeentchian Lord of Change Sheerargetru in the Black Fire Pass during the civil strife of the Turmoil of 2512 IC, the true Ghal Maraz was discovered and quickly returned to Karl Franz, who has wielded it ever since.

Very few knew of the replacement, as not only were the abilities of Ghal Maraz considered a state secret within the Empire, the creation of the replacement was another great secret tightly held by Karaz Ankor, who did not inform their Human allies of the exchange.

entries.name: Gnoldron
entries.text:
A Runic Hammer created by the Runesmith Arnek Ragasson during the War of Vengeance, translated from Khazalid as ‘Old Thunder’. Reputed to be the favoured hammer of the Funimrik clan of the Karak Vlag Runesmith craft guild, the weapon gained fame through numerous conflicts, attributed with the destruction of the gates of many Elf strongholds and with taking the heads of numerous war bosses in skirmishes against the Greenskin foe. The greatest tale told of the warhammer would be its use in the slaying of the dragon Ioridrak by the Runesmith Chrobak Ironarm, who is said to have spent weeks carefully crafted his own specialised equipment, carving into it a number of runes aimed specifically at his quarry. He made and used a cloak brooch with the Rune of the Furnace, a ring with the Rune of Healing should the battle be drawn out and boots with the Rune of Lightfoot, should the large size of his adversary cause his footing to be lost.

The hammer itself is said to be capable of throwing bolts of lightning at distant targets, and emitting a crack of thunder with each hit it delivers. There are also old mentions of the weapon granting the wielder protection from similar forms of magic. No known Master Rune that exists today is capable of these feats, implying that the one engraved into Gnoldron has been lost to time. For obvious reasons, information on the weapon is frequently sought by those versed in the research of Runes, hoping to uncover the weapon and its secrets.

The last confirmed report of the armament in Dwarven possession was in the hands of Runesmith Tudnak Haudssen at the time of the last incursion of Chaos into Karak Vlag, when it fell. All traces of the Dwarf hold and those that called it home disappeared, and it was believed that the weapon shared the same fate.

Many years passed until, just over a century ago, a band of Kislevite trappers operating near the Worlds Edge Mountains encountered a band of Tainted Dwarves. The trappers engaged them in combat, but were massacred to a man. The lone survivor of the trappers, one Ivan Keanovich, escaped to report the encounter and claimed that the leader used an ornate warhammer that could call forth lightning bolts at will.

An Imperial explorer named Tomas Ostermann came upon a copy of the report and determined that what was essentially a footnote of the retelling was enough to confirm that the weapon used was indeed Gnoldron, and he mounted an expedition to attempt to recover the weapon. His journal, which included an accounting of his investigation and preparation for the expedition, was left with the Temple of Verena in Middenheim. Unfortunately, Tomas was never heard from again.

Though his reasons for the expedition and what he sought to gain were not amongst his entries, the hammer would easily win its finder a lord’s ransom from any Dwarf King or Rune Lord for its safe return. The chance to find such a treasure has been a cause for no few groups of adventurers making their ways toward Kislev and looking for signs of Tainted Dwarf bands in the mountains to its east.

entries.name: Grimmaz
entries.text:
Grimmaz is a Rune Axe, also called “the Harsh Master”. Another weapon crafted during the War of Vengeance, in this case for the Jarlki clan, a ruling clan of Karak Ungor. It is said to have the power to increase the speed and fury of its bearer’s attacks. Additionally, it is also believed that the axe has the ability to destroy an opponent’s weapon regardless of its own enchantments.

It was used to great effect by Grim Jarlki and gained fame during the storming of the last Elf colony in the Old World at the site of present-day Marienburg. Following the fall of their Dwarf hold Karak Ungor in -1500 IC the Jarlkis, like many other noble clans, found refuge in Karaz-a-Karak.

Reclamation of the axe has been one of the noted objectives of a number of attempts to retake the hold throughout the years. In –975 IC, King Snorri Morgrimson led the clans to attempt to capture Karak Ungor. This force met with some initial successes, and Strakerd Jarlki, head of the clan at the time, was tasked to hold the southern gate of the Karak while other Dwarven forces worked their way to infiltrate and clear the inhabitants.

An especially aggressive onslaught by Goblins of the Twisted Claw tribe was able to force Strakerd and his warriors from the gate, sealing the fate of those that had moved further in. Ordered by the Dwarf King to hold his position until reinforcements arrived, Strakerd took the loss of his fellow Dwarves as a personal failing and chose to ignore the command. Whether he wanted to redeem himself by reclaiming the gate and purge his shame through heroism, sought personal renown or simply fell foul of his own hubris is not recorded, only that he disobeyed his orders and would ultimately fall while attempting to breach the Goblin lines.

The contingent was forced back, and eventually retreated to Karaz-a-Karak.

In the closing stages of the Great War Against Chaos, around 2301 IC, King Belegar led a force of Karak Ungor Dwarves to again attempt to retake the Karak with the intention to use it as a base, as Skalf Dragonslayer had done with nearby Karak Azgal almost a millennia before. Again, the recovery of Grimmaz was considered an immediate objective. Again, the force would be unsuccessful. The occupying greenskins proved too numerous, and in the final skirmish Belegar was mortally wounded. The kingship fell upon his son, Ulfar. The fallen king was returned to Karaz-a-Karak, where he remains interred until the day that Karak Ungor is retaken.

Given the amount of time that has passed since the weapon was lost, there are a number of conflicting sightings or theories of where the Axe may be. Some claim that the Twisted Goblin tribe who captured it originally passed it to the more dominant Red Eye tribe, before they then traded it to the Hobgoblins east of the Worlds Edge Mountains. Other accounts have stated that it has been seen in the possession of a marauding band of Tainted Dwarfs found near the High (Belyevorota) Pass, northeast of Praag.

Prince Ulther, the most recent leader of the Karak Ungor Dwarfs and grandson of King Belegar, has issued a bounty for any information that may lead to the recovery of the legendary heirloom.

entries.name: Crafting Runes
entries.text:
Crafting a permanent magic rune requires a great deal of work and time — often days, weeks, or even years. Characters rarely have the opportunity to undertake labour of this magnitude in the field, and will more commonly work their trade by using the Forge Rune Endeavour between adventures.

To forge a rune, choose one of the runes or master runes you have learned through Talents. Runes are always forged onto an existing, physical item, so you need to already own, purchase, or steal the Trapping you’re inscribing the rune onto. Runesmithing also requires you to have your own Trade Tools (Smith), and access to a Workshop. If you don’t have your own Workshop, you can work in your mentor’s forge, or request access to a peer’s Workshop as a Minor Favour (WFRP Core Rulebook). The actual forging process is resolved as an Extended Test. You can make one Test per week or Endeavour — a Challenging (+0) Runesmithing Test if forging a rune, or a Hard (-20) Runesmithing Test if forging a master rune. The number of SLs required to complete the process is specified in the rune’s description.

If the Extended Test is successful, the rune is successfully inscribed upon the target Trapping, transforming it into a runic item. Runic weapons, armour, etc. all count as magical items.

entries.name: Rule of Three
entries.text:
No runic item can be inscribed with more than three runes. Unless the crafter is possessed of a once-in-a- generation talent, all Tests to inscribe a fourth rune onto an item automatically fail.

A runic item may be inscribed with duplicates of the same rune, unless it is a master rune (see the Rule of Jealousy). The runes listed below explain the effects of a duplicated rune upon a runic item. Note that the effects of duplicate runes on the same runic item stack, but effects of duplicate runes on different runic items do not — creatures are only affected by whichever runic item has the most versions of that rune.

entries.name: Flawed Creations
entries.text:
A proud Dwarf Runesmith would never intentionally forge a rune that had suboptimal or intermittent effects. However, mistakes can happen, and it is not uncommon for a rune to appear functional, but reveal its shortcomings in the heat of battle.

When you conclude a Forge Rune Endeavour, you may choose to introduce a Runic Flaw to the rune you’re crafting. This provides an immediate +5 SL towards the ongoing Extended Test. A rune can only have one Runic Flaw, and in most instances, it is only worth acquiring one if the rune is needed in time for the next adventure.

A Runic Flaw is slow to materialise, and the Runesmith may not realise they have made a mistake. However, the first time a completed rune with a Runic Flaw activates its effects during an adventure, roll 1d10 and consult the Runic Flaw table to determine its effects.

entries.name: Rule of Form
entries.text:
Each of the categories of rune have specific rules about what items they can be forged upon. This is mostly self- explanatory —a weapon rune cannot be forged upon a crown, and so on.

Furthermore, runes can only be applied to materials suitable for permanent inscription, typically metal, stone, or jewels. Runes cannot be traced in sand, or marked with chalk, or painted on a wall. Runes cannot be forged on magical items, except those already marked with a Dwarfen rune magic. It is very rare for a rune to be forged upon an object not crafted by Dwarfen hands.

Runesmiths seldom experiment with new uses for their craft, but if a Character wants to bend the Rule of Form slightly — e.g. affixing a weapon rune to a spear, a talismanic rune to a cloak, or an engineering rune to a flame cannon — the GM may allow them to proceed with a negative modifier on their Runesmithing Tests.

entries.name: Runic Flaws Table
entries.text:
| 1d10 | Runic Flaw |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | The rune functions as intended for the next minute… after which, the runic item is consumed by its improperly contained power, destroying the Trapping and all runes it currently bears. |
| 2-3 | The rune functions as intended for the next minute, before its power is exhausted and dispersed into the Winds of Magic. The rune is destroyed, and must be forged from scratch. |
| 4-5 | The rune functions as intended for the rest of the adventure, before it fades and loses its power, and must be forged from scratch. |
| 6-8 | The rune inflicts 1 point of Damage upon the Trapping it’s inscribed upon. It inflicts 1 additional point of Damage upon the runic item at the start of each adventure. |
| 9-10 | The rune is sluggish to activate — whenever the bearer wishes to use its effects, they must spend 1 Fortune point to do so. |

entries.name: List Of Runes
entries.text: A Character can learn any of the runes in this list using the Runic Magic or Master Rune Magic (page 80) Talents.

entries.name: Armour Runes
entries.text: Armour runes can only be forged upon a Gromril Suit (page 95). If a Character is also wearing a Gromril Helm, Open or Closed, the armour rune extends its benefits to the helm as well.

entries.name: Protection Runes
entries.text: Protection runes can only be forged upon items of communal significance, such as religious icons, ale kegs, war banners, or permanent installations (sculptures, gatehouses, etc.). Their creation blurs the line between craft and ceremony, and is often undertaken by a priest of the Ancestor Gods. Unlike other runes, which only apply their effects to the bearer, a Protection Rune’s range of effect extends 6 yards, affecting any Dwarf allies within range. Especially well-displayed Protection Runes may extend their benefit further, at the GM’s discretion.

entries.name: Doom Runes
entries.text:
Doom runes can only ever be struck upon an Anvil of Doom (page 97). Crafting a Doom Rune does not require access to a Workshop, nor any materials besides Trade Tools and the Anvil itself. Given how precious an Anvil of Doom is, though, gaining access to use one is a difficult enough task in itself

Any Character who has learned a Master Rune also learns all three Doom Runes. Instead of an Extended Test, Doom Runes are activated as an Action, requiring a Hard (–20) Runesmithing Test. The effects of a Doom Rune can be Dispelled (WFRP Core Rulebook) as though they were a spell.

entries.name: Grungni — Cult Runic Magic
entries.text: Priests of Grungni may inscribe the following runes: Alarm, Blasting, Enemy Detection, Forging, Furnace, Preservation, Purification, Verminkill, Warding, Warmth, Warning, and Water.

entries.name: Grungni — Strictures
entries.text:
Through the quality of your gem cutting, your smithing, your brewing, and your masonry, uphold the glory of clan and hold.

Strive to ensure that each passage and hallway you construct is sound enough to endure the ages.

By hammer and by hand, mend what is broken.

Extract from the ground all the riches that are given to the Dawi.

Never squander the wealth gemstones and gold may grant you and your legacy.

Never surrender to Orcs, Goblins, or their kin.

Wherever our lands have fallen to our enemies, strive to reclaim them with axe and hammer.

entries.name: Valaya — Cult Runic Magic
entries.text:
Priests of Valaya can inscribe the following runes: Alarm, Battle, Enemy Detection, Healing, Light, Preservation, Purification, Resistance, Restoration, Sanctuary, Silence, Slowness, Spell Breaking, Verminkill, Warmth, Warning, Water

A High Priest of Valaya can also inscribe the Master Rune of Valaya.

entries.name: Valaya — Strictures
entries.text:
Always provide aid to a wounded or ailing Dawi.

Always assist a Dwarf-friend in need.

Always tend to the needs of the young Beardlings.

Defy our enemies in battle, defend your hold with honour.

Always keep ale and a warm fire for honoured guests.

Never allow the relics and treasures of our holds to fall into the hands of enemies, unless to do so saves Dawi lives.

entries.name: Grimnir — Cult Runic Magic
entries.text: Priests of Grimnir can inscribe the following runes: Battle, Breaking, Clear Seeing, Cleaving, Courage, Cutting, Farseeing, Fear, Fury, Might, Signalling, Silence, Slowness, Smiting, Striking, Warning

entries.name: Grimnir — Strictures
entries.text:
Obey the command of the Longbeards.

Stand solid as stone before the brutal foe and do not retire from the field of battle until its end.

Slay the enemies of the Dawi wherever you may find them.

Strive to slay monstrous foes of the Dawi wherever they encroach on our holds and deeps.

entries.name: Gazul / Smednir — Cult Runic Magic
entries.text: Priests of Smednir may inscribe the following runes: Cleaving, Cutting, Fate, Fire, Forging, Furnace, Iron, Silence, Smiting

entries.name: Gazul / Smednir — Strictures
entries.text: Defy the tomb robber, ghoul, and necromancer, for they are enemies to be despised. Honour our dead, protect their spirits and guard their reputations. Respect the dignity of the ancestors, to disturb their resting places is a heavy matter.

entries.name: Gazul / Smednir — Strictures
entries.text: Strive always to produce your best work. Labour not for those unworthy of the craft of the Dawi. Prize and protect your tools and forge as you would your greatest treasure.

entries.name: Thungni / Morgrim — Cult Runic Magic
entries.text: Priests of Thungni rarely inscribe runes, leaving such tasks to runesmiths. Should there be a need, priests are restricted to the following: Alarm, Communication, Disclosure, Enemy Detection, Luck, Sanctuary

entries.name: Thungni / Morgrim — Cult Runic Magic
entries.text:
Priests of Morgrim may inscribe the following runes: Accuracy, Alarm, Burning, Clear Seeing, Disguise, Enemy Detection, Farseeing, Forging, Fortune, Furnace, Immolation, Penetrating, Reloading, Seeking, Signalling

High Priests of Morgrim may inscribe the Master Rune of Defence.

entries.name: Thungni / Morgrim — Strictures
entries.text: Treasure the secrets of runecraft as carefully as you treasure gold. Sooner see your work destroyed than fall into enemy hands. Reclaim those items of runecraft that are wielded by those unworthy of them. Where our secrets are possessed by those unworthy of them, see to it that our secrets perish with them . You will be judged by your work, so strive to be the best.

entries.name: Thungni / Morgrim — Strictures
entries.text: Always seek redress from those who steal our secrets. Make your craft precise, and effective in its function. Innovate, but be cautious as you go. Ambition should not come at the detriment of craft. All engineering knowledge is sacred and must be preserved, even at the cost of novel concepts.

entries.name: Ancestors — Strictures
entries.text: Always honour one’s ancestors on every Day of Remembrance. Never perform or permit an act that brings dishonour to the memory of a clan ancestor. Always seek the guidance of an ancestor before any great undertaking.

entries.name: Sea Guard

You lose –3 Yenlui. 0 +8 SL — Immediately upon casting, you create a Magic Portal anywhere within Willpower Bonus yards. You must open the portal in a solid terrain feature. entries.text: Sacrifice: Extended Difficult (-1 SL) Research Test to a total of 20 SL You cast protective enchantments on an area. A designated password may exempt targets from the ward effect. Choose one of the following effects, applied to anyone entering the Area of Effect: 0 Forgetfulness: Memories from the last 24 hours are lost. 0 Purity: Suffer (Mutations x 6) Damage ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Daemons cannot enter the Area of Effect. 0 Surveillance: You can see the space within the Area of Effect by spending a Round to concentrate. 0 Truthfulness: No lies can be spoken within the Area of Effect. This spell can only be cast once on a given area. You can renew this spell with a CN 0 Casting Test before expiry, at the original Area of Effect, duration, and effects. Overcasting: To benefit from Overcasting options for this spell, your Yenlui State must be Light. +6 SL — Duration can be increased to Intelligence Bonus weeks. Esoteric faith spell: a Mage needs a tutor or access to pertinent reading materials (p. 99). Sacrifices and referenced external creature/ship profiles remain GM references.

entries.name: Soulcraft
entries.text: You bind a Ghost into a waystone or leyline. The entity and vessel must both be within range when the spell is cast. Mortals who have died within the last hour can have their ghosts bound into a vessel before they depart for the spirit realm. The purpose of doing so is usually to spare the soul from eternal suffering in the Realms of Chaos, or to prevent their souls being claimed by the Pale Queen. Should the Ghost not wish tto be bound in this manner, it may Oppose your Casting Test with its Cool, effectively increasing the spell’s CN by 1 for every SL it scores. Esoteric faith spell: a Mage needs a tutor or access to pertinent reading materials (p. 99). Sacrifices and referenced external creature/ship profiles remain GM references.

entries.name: The Primary Words

You can communicate on a basic level with any mortal creature or animal. Conveying or understanding advanced concepts might require an Intelligence Test by one or both parties. The exchange sounds like gibberish to bystanders unless they know Anoqeyån, in which case an Average (+2 SL) Language (Magick) Test allows them to comprehend the gist of it. Overcasting: To benefit from Overcasting options for this spell, your Yenlui State must be Light. 0 +2 SL — Allows advanced communication with elder species that predated the Old Ones, such as Dragons, Great Eagles, Fimir, and most animals. 0 +4 SL — Allows basic communication with any spirit, elemental, or Daemon. entries.text: You move with precision through a sequence of thirty intricate forms, gradually entering a meditative trance over several minutes. You may adjust Yenlui depending on the time the ritual is performed: towards Light at sunrise and toward Dark at sunset.

entries.name: Flight of the Phoenix
entries.text: With a swift spin, you pivot on the spot, launching your sword in a devastating throw with the grace of a Phoenix taking flight. The blade flies SB + WPB yards and strikes with your weapon’s Damage. The attack has the Penetrating Quality and each +1 SL increases the range and Damage by 1. You cannot use this technique while Engaged.

Any successful strikes on opponents over a period of Weapon Skill Bonus Rounds ignore 1 AP . Critical Wound table rolls are increased by +10 for the duration for each +1 SL on your Sword-dancing Test.

You may Oppose all missile attacks with Melee (Two-handed) over Initiative Bonus Rounds, increased by 1 Round for each +1 SL on your Sword-dancing Test. The target immediately suffers 10 + Sword-dancing SL Damage (ignoring Armour, but not TB) and receives 2 Deafened Conditions from the pain. Targets slain by this technique crumple to the ground with blood oozing from their ears. Each +1 SL on your Sword-dancing Test may increase the range and number of targets by 1.

Ithilmar Armour: The greatest of the steam-clad Dragon Spine Mountains is the volcano called Vaul’s Anvil, legendary seat of the god of smiths. The world’s only vein of ithilmar is found there. The Elves do not mine the volcano’s slopes but retrieve chunks of ithilmar ore that are shaken loose by tremors.

Ithilmar means ‘sky silver’ as it is light, gleaming, and incorruptible, but is also translatable as ‘star steel’, which speaks to its durability. The secrets of properly forging ithilmar are carefully guarded by the smith-priests of Vaul. Over the centuries, many pieces of ithilmar armour have been forged, and those made in the time of Aenarion can be as strong and gleaming as those that are newly forged.

Whilst Ithilmar Armour is light, it is still bulky, and thus a piece of Ithilmar Plate incurs a minimum Enc of 1 when carried rather than worn.

Prices for Ithilmar Plate are given, though it may also be used for the forging of scale, chain, or barding for horses. Ithilmar Armour pieces are always Unique Availability and massively expensive. To work out the price of a piece of Ithilmar Armour, take the listed price for the regular equivalent and double it seven times (multiply it by 128). So a Mail Coif from the WFRP Core Rulebook with a cost of 1 GC would be 128 GC if made from ithilmar, a set of Plate Bracers with a cost of 8 GC would be 1024 GC, and so on. We have worked out the price of common ithilmar items in the table above.

Dragon Armour: This magical mail is also forged in the weapon shops of Vaul’s Anvil. It is made of specially crafted enchanted steel that is magically resistant to extremes of heat. Only pieces of plate armour can be Dragon Armour.

If Dragon Armour is worn on a Hit Location that is struck by an attack that would inflict an Ablaze Condition, the Condition is not inflicted. If a Character wearing a full suit of Dragon Armour encounters a circumstance that would see them suffer Ablaze Conditions regardless of Hit Locations, they are protected, but a Character wearing partial Dragon Armour would not be.

Furthermore, the armour offers a great deal of protection against attacks that inflict Damage due to them being hot. If an attack is heat-based in any way — such as a Dragon’s Fire Breath attack or a spell from the Lore of Fire — then any Hit Location protected by Dragon Armour benefits from the following:

If the attack is noted as ignoring armour, it may not ignore Dragon Armour.

The Dragon Armour’s AP is doubled against that attack.

Dragon Armour may also provide protection against other forms of heat or fire at the GM’s discretion. Whilst it protects the wearer from short blasts of direct heat, it does not prevent them suffering from lack of air, poisonous fumes, or blinding smoke. A wearer of Dragon Armour still suffers from extreme heat exposure, and if they remain within a hot environment there is only so much the armour can do — a wearer of Dragon Armour could stand to be splashed with hot lava, but they could not go swimming in the caldera of an active volcano.

Dragon Armour pieces are always Unique Availability and massively expensive. To work out the price of a piece of Dragon Armour, take the listed price for the regular equivalent and double it ten times (multiply it by 1024). So a Helm from the WFRP Core Rulebook with a cost of 3 GC would be 3072 GC as Dragon Armour, a Breastplate with a cost of 10 GC would be 10240 GC, and so on.

White Lion Cloak: The White Lions are fierce predators that roam the wilds of the northernmost kingdoms, particularly Chrace. Their pelts are famed for their thick hides and heavy coats of hair, and can provide a degree of protection. Whilst some White Lion cloaks make it to market, it ought to be noted that in Chrace it is considered vulgar to wear one unless the wearer hunted and slew the White Lion from which the pelt was taken.

entries.name: Herbs and Elven Markets
entries.text:
The High Elves are well-versed in the use of herbs and wild plants to supplement their diet and help with healing or restorative practices. The ready availability of herbs in Ulthuan’s markets means that they are among those items that are more commonly available and sometimes cheaper than they are in the Old World.

The following table gives a revised list of prices and Availability for herbs and related products from the Consumer Guide in the WFRP Core Rulebook in Ulthuan.

Certain items are not available in Ulthuan, however. Map Cap Mushrooms, Ranald’s Delight, and Spit are made from ingredients that aren’t found in the Elven kingdoms, and there is insufficient demand to justify their importation.

Heartleaf: A dried halm of this herb gives off a pungent smell and fierce bright light when burned. Dragons find the light and the smell stimulating, so the herb is used by the dragonriders of Caledor to rouse their mounts from sleep or summon them to war. A Dragon that inhales the fumes of burning Heartleaf loses 1 Fatigued Condition.

If Heartleaf is burned where an awakened Dragon can see it or smell it, the Dragon is immediately aware of it. If that Dragon has a history of cooperation with Elves, they know the burning herb is intended to attract their attention and may act accordingly. Even if a Dragon is well-disposed to Elves they may resent being roused, especially if those who sought their attention do not treat them respectfully, expect them to act against their own interests, or do not have a serious reason for interacting with them. Wild or hostile Dragons are unlikely to be friendly if Heartleaf is used to attract their attention.

Narinocha Wine: During the reign of Caradryel, Aevin Thornchanter was transformed into a narinocha plant while attempting to harness the Wind of Ghyran. 750 years later, Alaesir Greydawn dispelled the magic holding Aevin in plant form. The pair used their combined learning to produce a wine fermented from narinocha pods that proved popular in the courts of Ulthuan. It is one of several wines Elves enjoy that instead induce feelings of relaxation and vivid visions.

When imbibing a glass of Narinocha Wine, a drinker must make a Challenging (+0) Consume Alcohol Test. Those who fail the Test suffer from the effects of alcohol as normal, but any Elves called upon to roll on the Stinking Drunk table use the alternative results given here.

entries.name: Narinocha Wine
entries.text:
| 1d10 | Effect of Narinocha |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Reassuring Mirage. Gain Yenlui (Light). Until you sober up, Perception Tests suffer from –1 SL. |
| 3–4 | Disquieting Illusion. Gain Yenlui (Dark). Until you sober up, Perception Tests suffer from –1 SL. |
| 5–6 | Kaleidoscopic Confusion. Until you sober up, Perception Tests suffer from –4 SL. |
| 7–8 | Vision of the Annuliis. Gain Yenlui (Balanced). |
| 9 | Dream of Bucolic Avelorn. Gain Yenlui (Dark). Until sober, Perception Tests suffer from –2 SL. |
| 10 | Nightmare of Mirai. Gain Yenlui (Dark). Until you sober up, Perception Tests suffer from –2 SL. |

Sunroot Extract: This health tonic does much to fortify the constitution, but only regular consumption can be shown to be beneficial. A vial contains ten doses, one of which may be added to a glass of spring water in order to create a refreshing drink. If a Character drinks, for the following week they benefit from a +20 bonus to any Tests to resist contracting a disease.

Viridescent Palliative: This pale green liquid is consumed by Elves in order to calm their desires. Each vial contains one dose of the palliative. After drinking, for the following 12 hours, an Elf experiences the following effects:

May not enter Frenzy

Yenlui becomes Balanced

May not benefit from any bonuses (but may ignore any penalties) resulting from a Dream or Obsession

May reroll failed Cool Tests to avoid Fear or Terror

Must ignore Prejudice, Animosity, or Hatred

entries.name: Enchanted Items
entries.text:
Whilst serious magical artefacts and weapons usually involve expensive and exacting craftsmanship of a High Elf mage or priest of Vaul, there are some items bearing petty enchantments that turn up for sale at Elven markets.

| Item | Cost | Enc | Availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ENCHANTED ITEMS |  |  |  |
| Aethyrolabe | 350 GC | 1 | Exotic |
| Flamespyre Phoenix Feather | 300 GC | 0 | Exotic |
| Frostheart Phoenix Feather | 400 GC | 0 | Exotic |
| Staff of Nightelm | 500 GC | 1 | Exotic |
| Staff of the Eternal Grove | 350 GC | 1 | Rare |
| Wayshard | 700 GC | 0 | Rare |

0 Rare Wayshard

Aethyrolabe: A device of interlocking brass discs and crystal lenses that is made by mages at the White Tower of Hoeth. The user of an Aethyrolabe can discern the relative concentrations of the Winds of Magic in a given area on a Challenging (+0) Lore (Magic) Test. They may also use the device to point to the nearest concentration of a particular Wind on a Hard (-20) Lore (Magic) Test.

Flamespyre Phoenix Feather: A feather plucked from a Flamespyre Phoenix will continue to burn brightly for about a year, making them prized by those who wish to use them as sources of illumination or combustion. The feather casts light with the same degree of intensity as a lantern, and may set things ablaze as effectively as a torch.

Frostheart Phoenix Feather: A feather plucked from a Frostheart Phoenix remains freezing cold for about a year. They cast a dim, cold light that provides the same sort of illumination as a candle and radiate sub-zero chill that refrigerates with the same efficacy as a brick of ice.

Mages, adventurers, and members of cults of pleasure prize Phoenix feathers, though how to safely transport them is a problem left to the buyer.

Staff of Nightelm: Groves of nightelm trees once flourished throughout the realm of Ellyrion but most of them were destroyed during the earliest days of strife between Asur and Druchii. Staffs of Nightelm are said to protect their bearers from hostile magic. If the bearer of a staff is targeted with any spell from the Lores of Witchcraft, Daemonology, Necromancy, Dark Magic, or any Chaos Lore, the bearer counts as having the Magic Resistance 3 Creature Trait. These staffs are sometimes used as the shafts for polearms.

Staff of The Eternal Grove: The trees of the Eternal Grove of Eataine are bathed in the Winds of Magic. They grow slowly and produce wood of exceptional hardness, so much so that those carpenters who work it must go to tremendous efforts to shape the wood. Any attempts to craft an item from the wood suffer from a penalty of –4 SL. Polearms and bows made from a Staff of the Eternal Grove possess the Durable 4 Quality.

Wayshard: Wayshards are either the remains of waystones that were shattered, or small pocketable waystones in and of themselves. These shards contain the essence of Elven soulstuff to keep them safe from predatory gods, and they would only be sold to an individual who could be trusted to keep them secure and protected from those who would defile them. Wayshards can be used to find a way to the nearest waystone, and are commonly used to navigate the mists of Yvresse. A bearer of a wayshard may use it to aid in Yenlui meditation (page 46) and may make a Challenging (+0) Pray Test in order to sense the direction of the nearest waystone.

entries.name: Dragonblade Ram
entries.text: A dragonship has one dragonblade ram on each prow. These ancient rams are forged from truesilver, tempered with dragonfire, and shaped by priests of Vaul. With the weight of the ship behind them, they can easily shear through the hull of an enemy vessel. The dragonship has an effective 15 AP to protect against Damage resulting from a frontal collision. If it causes a head on collision, add 20 to its Toughness Bonus when calculating its Collision Rating.

entries.name: Tracking Yenlui
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
Yenlui is tracked as a Psychology Trait. If an Elf behaves with moderation or balances the light and dark sides of their nature, there is no need to note Yenlui. However, if an Elf behaves in an extreme manner, their Yenlui may be recorded as either Yenlui (Light), Yenlui (Balanced), or Yenlui (Dark), depending on the behaviour exhibited.

The GM may decide that Yenlui is altered as the result of a dramatic act. They may also review an Elf ’s general behaviour at the end of each month or at the commencement of any downtime period and adjust Yenlui accordingly. Certain spell effects may only work if a Character is in a particular State, or may oblige them to move to another State.

entries.name: The Effects of Yenlui
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
Should an Elf attain a Yenlui State, they will suffer from the modifiers given in the table below. Note that there are some benefits to attaining a particular Yenlui State, though they tend to be in the performance of specific Skills or spells.

Yenlui (Light) You risk becoming jaded or fatalistic by overexposure to the light of the Cadai. This can be portrayed as a tendency towards indecisive, aloof, or insensitive behaviour.

Yenlui (Dark) You have become wicked or deviant by overexposure to the darkness of the Cytharai. This can be portrayed as a tendency towards sadistic, wanton, or sociopathic behaviour.

entries.name: Benefits of Obsession
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
Once per session, a player may point out that passing or failing a Psychology Test would go against the spirit of their Obsession. Provided the GM agrees, the player may decide on the result of that Psychology Test without needing to roll.

Example: The High Elf Eiloran has an Obsession to see the Dark Elves vanquished. During a session, a Dark Elf corsair uses Intimidate to cause Fear in Eiloran. Eiloran’s player points out that succumbing to this runs counter to her Obsession. The GM agrees that there is no need to Test.

entries.name: Example Obsessions
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
| 1d10 | Obsession |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | To leave an artistic or scholarly legacy. This involves the planning and creation of a great magnum opus that will find admirers for centuries to come. |
| 2 | To see the Dark Elves defeated once and for all. To convince other High Elves that Ulthuan’s military needs to be reinforced to meet this goal. |
| 3 | To ensure that a particular kingdom becomes the paramount realm in Ulthuan. This may involve rebuilding a shattered kingdom (such as Yvresse) or maintaining the power of an important kingdom (such as Eataine). |
| 4 | To reestablish High Elf dominions around the world. To convince other High Elves that Ulthuan’s navies must be reinforced to meet this goal. |
| 5 | To see that Ulthuan does not risk its people or its treasure in attempts to build alliances with Humans or Dwarfs. |
| 6 | To view sights no other Elf has seen by travelling to distant lands and exploring their remote regions. |
| 7 | To find someone in the world with whom you can fully relate through the forging of a solid friendship or true and lasting love. |
| 8 | To educate others in a system of thought that will lead them to live better lives in time to come. This may be a moral mission, one that seeks to wipe out a source of suffering, or the promotion of a form of pleasure-seeking. |
| 9 | To garner greater wealth and power with which to secure the safety and comfort of your family, friends, or neighbours. |
| 10 | To master your emotions, control your nature, and find inner peace. |

entries.name: Dreams
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
In Asur society, inclination toward prophetic dreams is common enough to be regarded as an acceptable eccentricity. Sensitivity to the Winds of Magic is widespread among Elves and often inspires such dreams since prognostication is carried on Azyr, the Blue Wind. Those with the favour of Lileath (or the less gentle attentions of Morai-Heg) may dream of the future, especially in times of crisis.

If a player and their GM agree, a High Elf can be inclined to Dreams. When this Character sleeps, the GM may decide that they experienced a significant Dream. This Dream should consist of simple, striking images that relate to but do not literally depict an upcoming challenge. If the Character chooses, they can replace their current Short- term Ambition with the Dream. Otherwise, it is forgotten.

When a Character encounters the situation foretold in their Dream, the GM should inform them that the Dream has come to pass. During the foretold events, any successful Tests made by the Character benefit from an additional +1 SL. The length of time this period lasts should be no shorter than an encounter and no longer than a day.

After a Character’s Dream comes true, they may choose a new Short-term Ambition at the end of the session.

Foreshadowed events should occur within the subsequent few sessions of gameplay. Since fate is a fickle thing, GMs are advised to describe Dreams that could be fulfilled in multiple ways. The table below provides a selection of Dreams and ideas about what they might mean.

entries.name: Negative Effects of Obsession
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
The GM may impose a penalty of –2 SL on any Test a Character takes that they feel ought to be compromised by the Obsession.

Example: After dealing with the Dark Elf sorceress, Eiloran is cornered by a trio of Dark Elves who threaten to run her through with their spears. Eiloran decides to see if she can use her Bribery Skill to persuade them to leave her alone. Because she has a Yenlui State of Yenlui (Balanced) the GM can impose negative effects of Obsession once for every time Eiloran benefited from Obsession. They, therefore, rule that the Bribery Test suffers from a penalty of –2 SL (in addition to any other modifiers they see fit to impose).

entries.name: Example Dreams
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
| 1d10 | Dream |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Teh land of Ulthuan is wracked by war, cities burn, and towers topple. To the south, the king and the general clasp their hands in friendship, and the Dragon takes filght. Tihs Dream recollects the story of Phoenix King Morvael and General Mentheus. Perhaps it urges the dreamer to delegate tasks to those more suited to them. It may warn that a friend faces peril or that disaster looms for the dreamer. |
| 2 | A war rages in the heavens. Two mighty fgiures wearing suits of black iron clash. After a great struggle, one is cast down, and the other yells in triumph. Tihs Dream refelcts Khaine’s victory over Vaul. It may portend that an attempt to exact vengeance will fail or warn that someone is trying to trap the dreamer. |
| 3 | You have served the master sculptor Oeric all your life. You watch in awe as he chisels fine detail into the hair of an Elf maiden made from bone white marble. The Dream may portend a dangerous temptation, the potential recovery of something thought lost, or the undertaking of a masterwork. |
| 4 | Storms lash at a high citadel on the northern coast of Ulthuan. A burning green witchfrie shines from the narrow windows in the tall towers. Flocks of harpies circle around its tallest towers, and waves crash at its base. A vision of the tower of Anlec may portend a building that contains great dangers or the fact that enemies are secretly mustering their strength to assail you. |
| 5 | Multicoloured winds cascade about you. You are tumbled about, spinning uncontrollably in the furious cyclone. Figures dressed in the panoply of mages folat within the tumult, their expressions calm and focused. Tihs vision of the Great Vortex may indicate that the dreamer must make a great sacrifcie to avert disaster or undertake a great or dangerous project. |
| 6 | A High Elf with noble bearing, wearing clothing that is expertly tailored but has clearly been worn in by years of travel, clasps hands with a Dwarf wearing the regalia of their high kings. Tehy smile in friendship. A vision of Malerion before he tried to claim the Phoenix Trhone, befriending the Dwarf high king Snorri Whitebeard. Perversely, this vision may portend either the chance to forge a valuable friendship or that someone close to you will betray you. |
| 7 | Teh Bloody-handed God rages. He has been tricked, and his precious treasures have been lost and scattered about, stolen and hidden in the mortal world, where the gods are forbidden to tread. Teh Dream may portend the loss or theft of a precious item or the chance to discover something that had been lost or stolen in the past. Alternatively, the Dream may warn that people who had previously seemed friendly may have changed their position, or that the dreamer should beware of a lover’s manipulations. |
| 8 | A fortress folats upon a dark sea. Chill winds blow, and mountains of ice drift through the water. Teh admiral aboard his dragonship orders his crew to close with the enemy and brace for a ram. The Dream suggests that a great victory may be won if the dreamer takes bold and decisive action. However, paradoxically, it may warn against overextending an effort and risking disaster if a consolidation of recent gains is not taken before greater victory is sought. |
| 9 | From their roosting sites among alabaster pillars of rock, gigantic birds with wings of falme take to the air, circling about and calling to one another with harsh cries. Tihs vision of Flamespyre Phoenixes may promise the dreamer an opportunity to reinvent themselves, fnid a new purpose in life, or cheat death. |
| 10 | Teh ancient Dragon struggles to rouse itself, but the temperature of the world is not to its liking. It shifts its weight onto its other side and yawns and falls to sleep once more. Teh Dream may warn that the dreamer is foolish to ignore a growing threat in favour of enjoying easy comforts. Alternatively, the Dream may hint that the current environment is not conducive to a hoped for course of action. |

entries.name: The Madness Of Khaine
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
| 1d100 | Mental Corruption |
| --- | --- |
| 01-20 | Hollow Heart |
| 21-40 | Profane Urgency |
| 41-60 | Thrill Hunter |
| 61-74 | Tortured Visions |
| 75-89 | Unending Malice |
| 90-00 | Unholy Rage |

You should discuss with your GM how to play your Character. Given they are over 16, they have likely attended the phoenix king and visited the Shrine of Asuryan. Your Character’s Mutation is, therefore, within the realms of normal Elven personality, if a little extreme at times. Commoners descended from Aenarion may not know of their heritage or may not have been scrutinised at 16.

Elves who know of your origins treat you differently to others. Suspicions could boil over into hostility, and some Elves see Aenarion’s descendants as inherently dangerous. These include the members of the secretive Cult of the Forbidden Blade, an order of duellists that aims to eliminate any who might take up the Widowmaker. Others may exalt you. Elves who want to revive the glory of Aenarion’s days may assume you share their ambitions and attempt to recruit you into their intrigues.

entries.name: Centuries of Experience
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
For each Time an Elder has lived through – not including the Time of Ending but including the Time of their birth – generate a Career that the Elder pursued during that Time. Use the Random Class and Career Table on page 59 or choose a Career available for your Character. If you choose a Career, you gain 10 Advances to spend on Skills available to the first level of that Career. If you generate a Career randomly, you instead gain 15 Advances. Either way, you cannot invest more than 5 Advances in any single Skill each Time.

In addition, for each Time you have lived through, you also gain Burdens. You gain the Burdens of all Times you have lived through, including the Time of your birth. However, Burdens relating to Yenlui are not cumulative. Instead, the Burden that relates to the earliest age applies.

Example: Kim is generating a Sea Guard Character, Seluin of Cothique. She decides to make Seluin an Elder, choosing for her to have been born in the Time of Voyages.

Kim generates a random Career for each of the three Times Seluin lived through (besides the Time of Ending). She gains the Smuggler Career for the Time of Voyages, the Herbalist Career for the Time of Incursion, and the Advisor Career for the Time of Steel. She spends 15 Advances each on the first level Skills of those different Careers. Although she cannot gain more than 5 Advances each Time for each Skill, the Perception Skill appears in both the Herbalist Career and the Advisor Career – she decides to take 5 Advances in the Skill each Time, giving her 10 Advances in Perception by the time she’s spent all her Elder Advances.

She gains Burdens associated with the Time of Voyages, the Time of Incursion, and the Time of Steel. The first Burden prevents her from taking more than 1 Endeavour each downtime. The second Burden gives her 5 Corruption. The third Burden means she only starts with 1 Extra Point for Fate and Resilience instead of 2. Kim knocks off the secondpoint of Fate she gave to Seluin in the Attributes step of Character creation. Finally, she must pass a Challenging (+0) Cool Test or gain the Yenlui (Light) Psychology Trait at the end of each week.

entries.name: Elders Of The Asur
entries.topic: High Elf creation, Careers and magic
entries.text:
The natural lifespan of Elves is far longer than Humans, Dwarfs, or Halflings, with some Elves appearing functionally immortal. Whilst the default age for High Elves is much older than other Characters, players may wish to play even older Asur. With experience comes wisdom and expertise, but also melancholy from witnessing their civilisation’s long, unavoidable decline.

During the Adding Detail step of Character creation (WFRP, pages 37-41) you may choose to play an Elder. Elder Characters have lived through spans of many years that correspond to a period of upheaval in Asur society. Decide which Time your Elder Character was born in and determine an age for your Character within that range. The Character has lived through all Times after the Time of their birth. For example, a Character born in the Time of Incursion has also lived through the Time of Steel and the Time of Ending.
